question: Who is the Title IX coordinator at Ramapo, and which office are they in?
good_reply: Kat McGee, J.D., Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance (the Title IX Coordinator): Office D 104, (201) 684-7220, kmcgee@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Leaving out the office when asked. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Title IX phone: (201) 684-7220. [1] Title IX is in D-104. [1] Title IX: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance: kmcgee@ramapo.edu To file a complaint at the College about an incident of discrimination and/or sexual misconduct: titleix@ramapo.edu [1]

Title IX's page "Who is the College’s Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator?" says: "Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)" [2]

Title IX's page "What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?" says: "The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. This includes management of grievances, investigations, and the disposition of complaints of sexual harassment, violence, rape, and discrimination under the Sexual Misconduct Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/))." (more on its page) [2]

Public Safety (Non-Emergency)'s page "Director of Title IX" says: "Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (“Title IX”) is a comprehensive federal law that prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex, or more specifically, discrimination on the basis of sex in any federally funded education program or activity. The Director of Title IX, also known as the Title IX Coordinator, is responsible for overseeing all Title IX reports of sexual discrimination, sexual assault and/or sexual misconduct. The Director of Title IX is also responsible for identifying and addressing any patterns of sexual discrimination and/or systemic problems that arise or is uncovered during the review of such reports." (more on its page) [3]

Office of the General Counsel & Institutional Compliance's page "Contact" says: "Nicole Morgan-Agard, Esq. Vice President and General Counsel E-mail: nmagard@ramapo.edu (mailto:nmagard@ramapo.edu) Phone: (201) 684-7503 Paul Szypiotko, Esq., LSW Assistant General Counsel E-mail: pszypiot@ramapo.edu Phone: (201) 684-7610 Stacy Storms Paralegal Email: sstorms@ramapo.edu (mailto:sstorms@ramapo.edu) Phone: (201) 684-7865 Kat McGee, J.D. value.heading: What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?
value.text: The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. The Director helps to ensure that all students, staff, administrators, and faculty are trained and educated about Title IX. The Director of Title IX is also responsible for identifying and addressing any patterns of sexual discrimination and/or systemic problems that arise or is uncovered during the review of such reports. question: how do i start my own club
good_reply: Through the Student Government Association: the SGA Vice President explains how to start a club, and SGA's Club Process & Allocations Committee reviews the proposed constitution and the Archway application. Contact sga@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Only how to join an existing club. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
1. Student Government Association: The Club Process & Allocations Committee, chaired by the Vice President, works with students who want to start new clubs on campus. Membership is limited to SGA members and club/organization leaders. [1]
2. Student Government Association: After the Vice President instructs them on how to start a new club, the Committee reviews the proposed constitution and Archway application. [1]
3. Center for Student Involvement: If you browse the list and find your interests are not represented, inquire at the Center about starting a new club or organization. [4]
4. Center for Student Involvement: Once the College recognizes an organization, it is eligible to receive financial support from the Student Activities Allocations Committee. [4]

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is a Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. Public policy examines how governmental laws and policies shape human lives; the program trains students in research methodologies, quantitative and qualitative methods, and skills for work with or for public institutions. [1]

Requirements: all of PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP. question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing track designed for registered nurses with an Associate's degree or Diploma in nursing. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. The Nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). Diploma-program graduates are granted 30 credits for their diploma nursing courses upon satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1]

Requirements:
- Required Math Course—select 1: MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; or SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY.
- RN to BSN Professional Core—required courses all of: NURS 312 NURSING INFORMATICS; NURS 316 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; NURS 330 HEALTH ASSESSMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; NURS 460 CLINICAL MANAGEMENT.
- Elective—select 1. Students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Other published levels include Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor consists of five courses (20 credits). [1]

- Required: BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY. It is 4 credits and requires BIOL 111 FUNDAMENTALS OF BIOLOGY I LECTURE to be complete. [1][3]
- Select 1 Statistics or Research Methods course: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS; MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS. [1]
- Select 1 Health Policy and Management course: COMM 383 THEORY AND PRACTICE OF HEALTH COMMUNICATION; ECON 332 HEALTH ECONOMICS: AN INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE; ENST 317 ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY AND REGULATION; MGMT 330 HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATION; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; or PUBL 201 PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC POLICY. [1]
- Select 1 Social and Behavioral Science course: SCIN 310 AIDS: BIOLOGICAL, MEDICAL, SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SWRK 230 AIDS: SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SWRK 328 COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH; PHLT 305 HEALTH AND WELLNESS; or PHLT 390 TOPICS. [1]
- Select 1 Global or Population Health course: ANTH 307 MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY; NURS 220 COMMUNITY HEALTH AND TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE; NURS 365 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; PHLT 290 TOPICS; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; or SPAN 311 SPANISH FOR HEALTH CARE AND HUMAN SERVICES PROFESSIONALS. [1]

NURS 425 requires the listed nursing prerequisites and corequisites; the catalog also lists a required course fee. [7]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-PHLT) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL204) [7](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/NURS425)

question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [13]:
- Friday, October 16, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade)

Registrar: If you complete the work by the completion date on the Incomplete Form or academic calendar, whichever is earlier, the assigned grade replaces the I. If the work is not satisfactorily completed by then, the grade changes to F. To request an incomplete, review the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for deadlines. The student and instructor must complete the Incomplete Form. [4]

1. Submit the form to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu). [4]
2. The Incomplete Request Form must reach the Office of the Registrar by the last day of the semester/session. [4]
3. In extraordinary circumstances, you may request an incomplete extension. [6]
4. The incomplete may only be extended until the end of the semester following the semester the incomplete grade was given. [6]
5. Get the incomplete extension form from the Office of the Registrar; it requires your signature and faculty approval. [6]
6. Submit the extension by the last day to resolve an incomplete grade listed on the Academic Calendar. [6]
7. Extension of an Incomplete Form ([https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Extension-of-an-Incomplete-Form-FILLABLE.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Extension-of-an-Incomplete-Form-FILLABLE.pdf)) [8]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [14]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/grading-options/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/grading-options/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/forms-transcripts/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
18 credits: In Fall and Spring, a matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester, at additional cost, must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit. [2] If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, they must get approval from their academic advisor before requesting the increase. [2] More than 20 credits requires approval from the student’s school Dean. [2] All matriculated undergraduate students should consult with the Office of Financial Aid before changing or exceeding credit load limits. [2] In Winter, students may register for a maximum of one course or 4 credits. [2]

[Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)] A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester. [7] A student can request more by applying for a credit overload. [7] To be granted the overload, the student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior. [7] The credit overload request form is here: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/). [7] The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student wishes to take more than the maximum for their program. [10] A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above. [10] Full policy details: [https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-load1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-load1). [10] Credit overloads will incur additional charges. Δ [10]

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [16]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [16]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#credit-load) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

pageFacts.question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it

facts.says: Fall and Spring A matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit.
If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar.
If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean.
All matriculated undergraduate students should consult with the Office of Financial Aid before changing or exceeding credit load limits.
Winter Students may register for a maximum of one course or 4 credits in the Winter session.
A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester.
However, a student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload.
The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload.
The credit overload request form can be found here (https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/).
The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program.
A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above.
Full policy details can be found by visiting the Credit Overload Policy (https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-load1).
Credit overloads will incur additional charges. Δ

pageFacts.question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it

facts.says: Fall and Spring A matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit.
If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar.
If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean.
All matriculated undergraduate students should consult with the Office of Financial Aid before changing or exceeding credit load limits.
Winter Students may register for a maximum of one course or 4 credits in the Winter session.
A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester.
However, a student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload.
The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload.
The credit overload request form can be found here (https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/).
The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program.
A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above.
Full policy details can be found by visiting the Credit Overload Policy (https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-load1).
Credit overloads will incur additional charges. Δ

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

**Office of the Provost**
Under some limited circumstances, a student may appeal a grade. Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case. Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy. Appeals that will not be considered include, but are not limited to, those based on a student’s perceived need for a higher grade (for instance, in order to raise their GPA or to enable the course to transfer to another institution) and those based on grades that were penalized (for example, a sanction of a 0 on an assignment or an F in the course) because the student was found responsible for violating the Academic Integrity Policy. [2]
If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter. Supporting documentation must be provided. Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion. Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade. If it is mutually agreed that a grade adjustment is warranted, the course instructor forwards an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request, including explanatory reasons and all supporting documentation, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course. Upon the Dean’s approval, the Instructor Grade Adjustment Request is forwarded to the Registrar. If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor. The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate. If the Dean determines that a grade change is warranted, the Dean will forward an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request with explanatory reasons to the Registrar and advise the course instructor and student in writing. If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email. [3]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [21]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [22]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Financial Aid: If you drop below full-time status, your financial aid will be adjusted. [1] Federal aid requires you to be enrolled in 6 credits in a semester. [1] If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits, your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans. [1] If you have state aid, it is subject to being canceled, and institutional grants and scholarships could also be reduced or taken away. [1] Federal aid should not be affected if a student is still enrolled for 6 or more credits. [2] NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires that students be enrolled full time at the time the aid is fully disbursed to your account. [2] If you drop below full-time status which is less than 12 credits, your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester. [3] Please contact the Office of Financial Aid to discuss your situation before making a change that drops you below full-time status for the semester. [3]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [12]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Orientation Programs

Graduate Admissions

question: im graduating in january, when is my graduation application due
good_reply: Nov 6, 2026 for the January 2027 conferral, still ahead on the day asked. The application goes through the Registrar.
must_not: A wrong date; calling the deadline passed.

body.answer:
Registrar: For a January graduation, applications and all paperwork are due November 6. [1] The Fall deadline is November 6; degrees are officially conferred January 23, and diplomas are mailed Mid-March. Spring applications are due April 1*; degrees are conferred June 20, and diplomas arrive Late July. Summer applications are due May 31*; degrees are conferred August 30, and diplomas arrive Late September. Applications received after March 30th will not be listed in the Commencement Program. [2] The fee will be added directly to your bill/account and due upon receipt. [2] Fall applications are available June 1 to November 6; the deadline is November 6, conferral is January 22, 2027, diplomas are mailed Mid-March, and the commencement date is To Be Announced. Spring applications are available October 15 to April 1; the deadline is April 1, conferral is June 17, 2027, diplomas are mailed Late July, and the commencement date is To Be Announced. Summer applications are available March 1 to May 31*; the deadline is May 31*, conferral is August 21, 2026, diplomas are mailed Late September, and the commencement date is To Be Announced. Applications received after April 1 will not be listed in the Commencement Program. [3]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/application-for-graduation/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

**Housing & Residence Life**
1. Register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS) to request specific housing accommodations for a medically related condition. [1]
2. Once affiliated, OSS will inform the Office of Residence Life of residents who need specific housing accommodations based on medical documentation provided to OSS. [1]
3. Submit housing accommodation requests no later than published deadlines. [1]
Phone 201-684-7514 Email: oss@ramapo.edu www.ramapo.edu/oss [1]

**Office of Specialized Services**
4. Students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with OSS. [3]
5. Students must initiate contact with OSS to receive services or arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [3]
6. Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations and/or adjustments. [3]
7. For a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor only, students do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms. [3]
8. Students in those cases only need to complete a request for disability support form. [3]
Housing accommodations are provided based on availability. [4]
Students can expect a decision within twenty one (21) business days of OSS receiving all requested documentation. [4]

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Office of Specialized Services: It depends. An emotional support animal may be on campus when a student with a disability has registered with OSS, provided disability documentation showing the animal’s benefits, and received an accommodation allowing the animal on campus. [2]
Student use may be limited to defined campus areas and generally is not permitted in academic or recreational facilities. [2] The College is committed to accommodating disabilities that require service or support animals. [3] Animals are allowed on campus only when providing service or support to a College member or campus guest as a reasonable disability accommodation. [3]
OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a request if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented. [4] OSS and the Committee determine whether the accommodation is reasonable. [4] It may be unreasonable if: 1) the documented condition does not rise to the level of a disability; 2) documentation does not adequately support the request; 3) it imposes an undue financial and or administrative burden on the college; 4) it fundamentally alters college housing policy; or 5) it poses a direct threat to others’ health and safety or would cause substantial property damage, including to college property. [4] For an emotional support animal request, the College may also ask about the animal’s age, size/breed, if applicable, to determine reasonableness. [4]
All students requesting a disability-based housing accommodation must first register for affiliation with OSS. [5] Students must initiate contact with OSS to receive services or arrange accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [5] Comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations and/or adjustments. [5]
Please call our office at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest in having an Emotional Support Animal on campus. [1] Interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director to discuss further. [1] Refer to the Emotional Support Animal Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/)) for more information. [1]

pageFacts.question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work

facts.says: Please call our office at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest in having an Emotional Support Animal on campus.
Interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director to discuss further.
Please refer to the Emotional Support Animal Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) for more information.

When a student with a disability has registered with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS), provided disability documentation demonstrating the benefits provided by the emotional support animal, and been granted an accommodation permitting the presence of the emotional support animal on campus.
Student use of emotional support animals may be limited to defined areas of campus and generally will not be permitted in academic or recreational facilities.
However, the College is also committed to accommodate students and others with disabilities that require the assistance of service or support animals.
Animals are only allowed on campus when they are providing service or support to a member of the College or guest to campus as a reasonable disability accommodation.
OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a requested accommodation if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented.
OSS together with the Housing Accommodation Request Committee shall determine if the requested accommodation is reasonable.

An accommodation may be deemed unreasonable if: 1) the student’s documented condition does not rise to the level of a disability; 2) documentation does not provide adequate evidence to support the request; 3) imposes an undue financial and or administrative burden on the college; 4) fundamentally alters college housing policy; 5) poses a direct threat to the health and safety of others or would cause substantial property damage to the property of others, including college property.
Regarding a request for an emotional support animal, if applicable the College may also inquire as to the age, size/breed of an animal in order to determine the reasonableness of this accommodation.
All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Students must initiate contact with OSS in order to receive services or to arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments.

Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted in order to establish eligibility and to determine which accommodations and/or adjustments are appropriate for each student.

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

Public Safety: An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the issuance of a citation. Appeal online via the form: [https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3) [1] Failure to file within twenty (20) days forfeits the right to appeal. [2] Appeals will not be considered for ignorance of the regulation, inability to find a legal parking space, operation of the vehicle by another person, failure of parking enforcement staff to ticket previously for similar offenses, inability to pay the fine, disagreement with Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations, or citations issued by the Mahwah Police Department. Identify the specific ground(s) and briefly describe the justification. [2]
During regular business hours, payments may be made to the Office of Student Accounts. [3] FIRST stop at the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, or contact parking services at parking@ramapo.edu, to ensure the fine has been transferred to your student account. [3] Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee. [3] The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days. [3] A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [3]
To pay online, use [https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). Enter Citation # and Fine Amount, search for the citation, select your citation and follow the field required. [4] Select Payment Method. Once processed your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid. [4]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [13]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS: Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee.
The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days.

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts: To view current, real-time account activity and balances, run an On-Demand Statement or view the eBill statement. The eBill is the place to designate third parties (i.e. parents) as Authorized Users to view the bill and make payments. It is the only place to make an online payment, such as a credit/debit card or ACH payment, enroll in a monthly payment plan, and access previous bills. [1]

1. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)). Locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab at the top of the page. Select the term, click Continue, choose Credit Card via PayPath from the Payment Method drop down, then click Select. Verify or modify the payment amount and click Continue to PayPath. Read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer on the Welcome to the PayPath Payment Service! [6]
2. On the Screen, click Continue. Review the payment amount information and click Continue. Enter all Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click Continue. All entered data, including the service fee amount charged by PayPath, will be displayed. [6]
3. The credit/debit card service fee is based on a rate of 3.0% with a minimum fee of $3.00. [6]
4. Review your entries. If any data is incorrect, click Change Information. To cancel the transaction, click Cancel. Click Submit to submit your payment. By submitting, you accept the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]
5. Verify your bank account routing and account number before submitting your payment. [7]
6. These payments can ONLY be made ON-LINE. [7]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

value.heading: Who is the College’s Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator?
value.text: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)

value.heading: What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?
value.text: The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. This includes management of grievances, investigations, and the disposition of complaints of sexual harassment, violence, rape, and discrimination under the Sexual Misconduct Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/). The Director of Title IX is responsible for monitoring the overall implementation of Title IX for the College and coordinating compliance efforts. The Director helps to ensure that all students, staff, administrators, and faculty are trained and educated about Title IX. The Director of Title IX reports to the Office of the General Counsel & Institutional Compliance.

question: is the honors dean in today? i need to drop off my application at his office
good_reply: Says it can't know who is in the office today. Names Interim Dean Michael Unger, Undergraduate Studies and Honors, ASB 123, and suggests checking before going.
must_not: Saying the dean is in or out; correcting or adding the dean's gender ("she", "not a man"). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
I can't see live updates, like the weather, closings or how busy a place is right now.

The Office of the Provost identifies Michael Unger as Interim Dean of Undergraduate Studies and Honors [15]. I can’t verify whether he is in today. The Registrar’s School Deans page lists his office as ASB 123 [6].

For current Ramapo first-year students applying after their first semester, the application page says the window is December 1 to January 8, and requires a 3.50 GPA from the Fall semester [9]. It says to email PDFs of the admission essay, one faculty recommendation, and a sample of work, with the headline “Honors Application”; the page gives eaugis@ramapo.edu as the email [9]. The catalog also says to send these materials to honors@ramapo.edu [17]. The pages differ on the email address. The page’s instructions specify email, not dropping it off in person [9][17].

For whether he is in today, contact the Office of the Provost. [15]

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [32]
- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [32]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/honors/applications/current-ramapo-students/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/) [17](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#college-honors-program1) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is the Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. Public policy examines how governmental laws and policies shape human lives; the program trains students in research methodologies, quantitative and qualitative methods, and skills for working with or for public institutions. [1]

Requirements: Required Courses all of: PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; and PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP. Electives: Select 3 at least 3 of: ACCT 502 GOVERNMENT AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ACCOUNTING; ACCT 625 INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING; BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS; BADM 503 BUSINESS LAW, ETHICS & REGULATORY PRONOUNCEMENTS; DATA 601 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE; DATA 670 DATA VISUALIZATION; MATH 570 APPLIED STATISTICS; MATH 685 INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; MBAD 610 BECOMING A 21ST CENTURY LEADER; MBAD 625 CRISIS & CHANGE MANAGEMENT; NURS 660 LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION IN HEALTHCARE; NURS 670 HEALTHCARE ECONOMICS AND FINANCE; NURS 808 HEALTH POLICY LEADERSHIP; MSWK 505 SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS AND POLICIES I; MSWK 507 CULTURAL DIVERSITY, RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; MSWK 604 ADVANCED SOCIAL POLICY; MSWK 610 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; MSWK 670 SOCIAL WELFARE POLICIES IN HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH. [1]

Other published options: Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor. [1]

The admissions page lists one letter of recommendation (professional or academic); enter references’ names and contact information in the online application’s “Recommendations” section, and Ramapo sends them an automated request to upload recommendations to the application portal. The letter is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent Ramapo graduates from 2025 and 2026. It also lists a 400-word personal statement describing why you are interested in the program, how it fits into personal intellectual development and what you expect to accomplish by enrolling, and a resume. [6]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing track for registered nurses prepared at the Associate’s degree or Diploma level. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Ramapo’s nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). [1]

Diploma-program graduates are granted 30 credits for diploma nursing courses upon satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1]

Requirements:
- Required Math Course — select 1: MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; or SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY.
- RN to BSN Professional Core — required courses all of: NURS 312 NURSING INFORMATICS; NURS 316 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; NURS 330 HEALTH ASSESSMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; NURS 460 CLINICAL MANAGEMENT.
- Elective — select 1. Students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Other published levels: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor (Minor) consists of five courses (20 credits). [1]

Requirements: BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY (required); select 1 Statistics or Research Methods course: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS; MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS. question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [17]:
- Friday, October 16, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade)

Registrar: If you finish the work by the completion date on the Incomplete Form or academic calendar, whichever is earlier, your assigned grade replaces the I. If you do not satisfactorily complete it by then, the grade changes to F. The student and instructor must complete the Incomplete Form. [4] Submit the form to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu). [4] The Incomplete Request Form must reach the Office of the Registrar by the last day of the semester/session. [4]

In extraordinary circumstances, you may request an extension. [6] It can only extend to the end of the semester following the semester the I was given. [6] Get the extension form from the Office of the Registrar; it needs your signature and faculty approval. [6] Submit it by the deadline to resolve an incomplete grade posted on the Academic Calendar. [6] Extension of an Incomplete Form ([https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Extension-of-an-Incomplete-Form-FILLABLE.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Extension-of-an-Incomplete-Form-FILLABLE.pdf)) [8]

Office of the Provost: An I is given in extenuating circumstances, such as illness or another emergency, when the instructor approves it and a student who has satisfactorily completed at least two-thirds of course requirements before the end of a term requests it on an Incomplete Request form. [14] The default coursework deadline is on the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for each semester—typically February 26 for fall semester incompletes and October 15 for spring and summer incompletes, or the next business day—but the instructor may set an earlier deadline when the I is requested. [14] If work is completed before the deadline, the instructor completes a Grade Adjustment Request form and the new grade replaces the I. If work is not satisfactorily completed by the deadline, the grade changes to F. You may not graduate with an I outstanding. [14]

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Office of the Provost: In Fall and Spring, a matriculated student who wants to register for more than 18 credits per semester, at additional cost, must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit. [2] If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor before making the request to the Office of the Registrar. [2] A student attempting to register for more than 20 credits must obtain approval from their school Dean. [2]

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester. [7] A student can request more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload. [7] The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload. [7] The credit overload request form can be found here ([https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/)). [7]

Registrar: The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student wishes to take more than the maximum for their program. [9] A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above. [9] Credit overloads will incur additional charges. [9]

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [16]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [16]

facts.says: Fall and Spring A matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit.
If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar.
If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean.
A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester.
However, a student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload.
The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload.
The credit overload request form can be found here (https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/).
The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program.
A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above.
Credit overloads will incur additional charges. Δ

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status. That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

Office of the Provost
Under some limited circumstances, a student may appeal a grade. [2] Grade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case. [2] Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy. [2] Appeals that will not be considered include, but are not limited to, those based on a student’s perceived need for a higher grade (for instance, in order to raise their GPA or to enable the course to transfer to another institution) and those based on grades that were penalized (for example, a sanction of a 0 on an assignment or an F in the course) because the student was found responsible for violating the Academic Integrity Policy. [2]

1. If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor. [3]
2. The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate. [3]
3. If the Dean determines that a grade change is warranted, the Dean will forward an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request with explanatory reasons to the Registrar and advise the course instructor and student in writing. [3]
4. If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email. [3]
5. The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination. [3]
6. If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost. [3]
7. The petition is initiated by the submission of a written statement by the student, submitted by email or certified letter, that explains their position and includes any evidence that contradicts the Dean’s decision or contains information that had heretofore been unavailable. [3]
8. Such a petition must be made within twenty calendar days of the final, written determination by the Dean. [3]
9. The Office of the Provost reserves the right to hear the petition and will reject any request that does not offer clear evidence that the Dean made a factual mistake, violated school policy, or otherwise acted outside the purview of the Dean. [3]
10. The Provost or their designee will consider only those grade appeals that have previously received full deliberative discussion at both the instructor and Dean level. [3]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [31]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [32]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [31](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Financial Aid: If you drop below full-time status, your financial aid will be adjusted. [1] Federal aid requires you to be enrolled in 6 credits in a semester. [1] If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits, your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans. [1] State aid may be subject to being canceled, and institutional grants and scholarships could also be reduced or taken away. [1] Federal aid should not be affected if you are still enrolled for 6 or more credits. [2] NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires that students be enrolled full time at the time the aid is fully disbursed to your account. [2] If you are considering withdrawing from any classes, it is highly recommended that you meet with the Office of Financial Aid to discuss if and how this may impact on your current aid package. [2] If you drop below full-time status, which is less than 12 credits, your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester. [3] Please contact the Office of Financial Aid to discuss your situation before making a change that drops you below full-time status for the semester. [3]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can i still add a class this semester
good_reply: No: the last day to add full-semester fall courses was Sep 1, 2026 (Session II: Oct 21). Winter classes start Dec 17 and Spring 2027 registration is open (since Oct 27).
must_not: Telling the student they can still add; leaving out that the deadline passed.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [11]:
- Friday, August 28, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Tuesday, September 1, 2026: Full Semester Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Thursday, December 17, 2026: Last Day to Add/Drop Winter Classes with 100% Tuition Refund (also on the Winter 2027 calendar)

Spring: application available October 15 to April 1; application deadline April 1; official conferral of degrees June 17, 2027; diploma mailed Late July; commencement ceremony date To Be Announced. Summer: application available March 1 to May 31*; application deadline May 31*; official conferral of degrees August 21, 2026; diploma mailed Late September; commencement ceremony date To Be Announced. *Graduation Applications received after April 1 will not be listed in the Commencement Program. question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

**Housing & Residence Life**
1. For specific housing accommodations due to a medically related condition, register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS). [1]
2. Submit housing accommodation requests by the published deadlines. [1]

**Office of Specialized Services**
3. Students requesting a disability-based housing accommodation must first register for affiliation with OSS. [3]
4. See “How To Request OSS Services” ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/)) for more information. [3]
5. Contact OSS to receive services or arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [3]
6. Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations and/or adjustments. [3]
7. A decision is expected within twenty one (21) business days after OSS receives all requested documentation. [4]
8. For a comprehensive description, see the OSS Housing Accommodation Request Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf)). [5]
9. See Housing Accommodations ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/)) for more information and necessary forms. [7]

good_reply: Yes, OSS serves students with temporary disabilities such as a broken limb: submit the Application for Disability Support and current documentation, then an intake meeting with the OSS Director or Assistant Director authorizes accommodations. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.

body.answer:

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.

body.answer:
It depends. Office of Specialized Services: Please call our office at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest in having an Emotional Support Animal on campus. [1] Interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director to discuss further. [1] Refer to the Emotional Support Animal Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/)) for more information. [1] A student with a disability must register with OSS, provide disability documentation demonstrating the benefits of the emotional support animal, and be granted an accommodation permitting it on campus. [2] The College is committed to accommodating students and others with disabilities who require service or support animals. [3] Animals are allowed on campus only when providing service or support to a College member or campus guest as a reasonable disability accommodation. [3] OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a requested accommodation if unreasonable or insufficiently documented. [4] OSS and the Committee determine whether it is reasonable. [4] It may be unreasonable if: 1) the student’s documented condition does not rise to the level of a disability; 2) documentation does not provide adequate evidence; 3) it imposes an undue financial and or administrative burden on the college; 4) it fundamentally alters college housing policy; 5) it poses a direct threat to others’ health and safety or would cause substantial property damage, including to college property. [4] For an emotional support animal, if applicable, the College may inquire about its age and size/breed to determine reasonableness. [4] Students requesting a disability-based housing accommodation must first register for affiliation with OSS. [5] Students must initiate contact with OSS to receive services or arrange accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [5] Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations and/or adjustments. When a student with a disability has registered with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS), provided disability documentation demonstrating the benefits provided by the emotional support animal, and been granted an accommodation permitting the presence of the emotional support animal on campus.

Regarding a request for an emotional support animal, if applicable the College may also inquire as to the age, size/breed of an animal in order to determine the reasonableness of this accommodation.
All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Students must initiate contact with OSS in order to receive services or to arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments.

Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted in order to establish eligibility and to determine which accommodations and/or adjustments are appropriate for each student.

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Public Safety: You have twenty (20) days from the citation’s issuance to appeal online through the form at [https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3). [1]

1. Submit the appeal within twenty (20) days; otherwise, you forfeit the right to appeal. [2] The College’s Parking Appeals Board reviews appeals regularly. [3] An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the citation’s issuance. [4] Appeals are also accepted through citation@ramapo.edu and reviewed regularly by the College’s Parking Appeals Board. [5] Appeals will not be considered for ignorance of the regulation, inability to find a legal parking space, operation of the vehicle by another person, failure of parking enforcement staff to ticket previously for similar offenses, inability to pay the fine, disagreement with Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations, or citations issued by the Mahwah Police Department. Identify the specific ground(s) and briefly describe your justification. [6]

2. During regular business hours, payments may be made to the Office of Student Accounts. [7] FIRST stop at the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, or contact parking services at parking@ramapo.edu to ensure the fine has been transferred to your student account. [8] Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee. [9] The ability to appeal is forfeited if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days. [10] A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [11]

3. Pay online at [https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). Enter Citation # and Fine Amount, search for the citation, select your citation, and follow the required fields. [12] Select Payment Method. Once processed, your citation will be emailed to you to say it is paid. [13]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [13]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [13]
- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [13]

facts.says: How to Appeal Your Parking Citation Click Here to Go to the Appeal Portal (https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3) Appeals are input online via the form An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the issuance of a citation.
Failure to file the appeal within twenty (20) days constitutes forfeiture of the right to appeal.
All appeals are are reviewed on a regular basis by the College’s Parking Appeals Board.
An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the issuance of a citation.
All appeals are accepted through citation@ramapo.edu (mailto:citation@ramapo.edu) and are reviewed on a regular basis by the College’s Parking Appeals Board.

Appeals will not be considered for: Ignorance of the regulation Stated inability to find a legal parking space Operation of the vehicle by another person Stated failure of parking enforcement staff to ticket previously for similar offenses Inability to pay the fine Disagreement with Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations Citations issued by the Mahwah Police Department Appellants must identify upon which specific ground(s) they are appealing and briefly describe their justification.
During regular business hours, payments may be made to the Office of Student Accounts.

You must FIRST stop at the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, or contact parking services at parking@ramapo.edu (mailto:parking@ramapo.edu), to ensure that the fine has been transferred to your student account.
IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS: Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee.
The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days.
A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days.

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts:
1. Run an On-Demand Statement and view the eBill statement to see current, real-time account activity and balances. Use the eBill statement to designate a third-party (i.e. parents) as Authorized Users to view the bill and make payments, make online payments such as credit/debit card or ACH payments, enroll in a monthly payment plan, and access previous bills. [1]
2. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)). Locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab. Select the term, click Continue, choose Credit Card via PayPath from the Payment Method drop down, and click Select. Verify or modify the payment amount, then click Continue to PayPath. Read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer on the Welcome to the PayPath Payment Service screen, then click Continue. [6]
3. Review the payment amount information and click Continue. Enter all Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click Continue. Review the displayed data, including the service fee amount charged by PayPath. [6]
4. The credit/debit card service fee is based on a rate of 3.0% with a minimum fee of $3.00. [6]
5. Review your entries. If any data is incorrect, click Change Information. To cancel, click Cancel. Click Submit to submit your payment; submitting accepts the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]
6. Verify your bank account routing and account number before submitting your payment. [7]
7. The Office of Student Accounts does not accept ACH payments by phone or in-person. [7]
8. These payments can ONLY be made ON-LINE. [7]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
