value.heading: Who is the College’s Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator?
value.text: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)

value.heading: What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?
value.text: The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. This includes management of grievances, investigations, and the disposition of complaints of sexual harassment, violence, rape, and discrimination under the Sexual Misconduct Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/). The Director of Title IX is responsible for monitoring the overall implementation of Title IX for the College and coordinating compliance efforts. The Director helps to ensure that all students, staff, administrators, and faculty are trained and educated about Title IX. The Director of Title IX reports to the Office of the General Counsel & Institutional Compliance.

value.heading: Contact Information for Reporting
value.text: Kat McGee, Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance (available during regular business hours) Phone: (201) 684-7220 Office Location: D-104 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu) The Public Safety Department (available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week) Phone: (201) 684-6666 Office Location: C-102 Handout: Title IX Reporting Requirements (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/wp-content/uploads/sites/300/2026/10/Title-IX-Reporting-Requirements-FY27.pdf)

value.heading: Reporting an Incident of Discrimination
value.text: Reporting an Incident of Discrimination To file a complaint at the College about an incident of discrimination, please contact: Kat McGee, Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office of the General Counsel & Institutional Compliance E-mail: kmcgee@ramapo.edu Phone: (201) 684-7220 Any student has the right to file a complaint with the Office of Civil Rights of the U.S. Department of Education. Questions about Title IX may be referred to the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights. To file a complaint with the Office of Civil Rights, please contact: U.S. Department of Education, Office for Civil Rights Lyndon Baines Johnson Department of Education Bldg 400 Maryland Avenue, SW Washington, DC 20202-1100 Telephone: 800-421-3481 FAX: 202-453-6012; TDD: 800-877-8339 Email: OCR@ed.gov (mailto:OCR@ed.gov) Ramapo College is an Institutional Member of the Student Conduct Institute – The State University of New York. View our campus TIX training (https://system.suny.edu/sci/postedtraining/).

value.heading: Director of Title IX
value.text: Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (“Title IX”) is a comprehensive federal law that prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex, or more specifically, discrimination on the basis of sex in any federally funded education program or activity. The Director of Title IX, also known as the Title IX Coordinator, is responsible for overseeing all Title IX reports of sexual discrimination, sexual assault and/or sexual misconduct. The Director of Title IX is also responsible for identifying and addressing any patterns of sexual discrimination and/or systemic problems that arise or is uncovered during the review of such reports. The Director of Title IX will supervise and coordinate all such reports to ensure a prompt, thorough and fair investigation and resolution process at the College. Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX, ADA and Compliance Training E-mail: kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu) Office: D 104 Phone: (201) 684-7220

value.heading: The Office of Title IX (NON-Confidential Resource)
value.text: Location: D-104 (near the Arch) Phone Number: (201) 684-7220 The Office of Title IX (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/) provides assistance navigating campus and community resources. Support can include: Help in identifying your immediate needs Referrals for counseling, advocacy, medical, and legal resources Issuing a “No Contact Order” Explaining your rights and resources for reporting sexual assault to law enforcement and/or College officials Requesting academic extensions or accommodations (such as assistance in transferring to another section of a course, assistance in requesting withdrawal or an incomplete grade in a particular course, leaves of absence or withdrawal from the College, or assistance requesting alternate methods of completing coursework) Assistance in relocating an on-campus housing assignment or campus job Increased security and monitoring of certain areas of the campus Arranging a meeting to discuss safety planning Providing step by step assistance with investigations under the Sexual Misconduct Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/) Providing financial aid-related information Transportation or parking accommodations Connecting you with a variety of other campus and community resources Students do not need to participate in an investigation or file charges in order to request support from the Office of Title IX.

value.heading: Director of Title IX
value.text: Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972 (“Title IX”) is a comprehensive federal law that prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex, or more specifically, discrimination on the basis of sex in any federally funded education program or activity. The Director of Title IX, also known as the Title IX Coordinator, is responsible for overseeing all Title IX reports of sexual discrimination, sexual assault and/or sexual misconduct. The Director of Title IX is also responsible for identifying and addressing any patterns of sexual discrimination and/or systemic problems that arise or is uncovered during the review of such reports. The Director of Title IX will supervise and coordinate all such reports to ensure a prompt, thorough and fair investigation and resolution process at the College. Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX, ADA and Compliance Training E-mail: kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu) Office: D 104 Phone: (201) 684-7220

value.heading: The Office of Title IX (NON-Confidential Resource)
value.text: Location: D-104 (near the Arch) Phone Number: (201) 684-7220 The Office of Title IX (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/) provides assistance navigating campus and community resources. Support can include: Help in identifying your immediate needs Referrals for counseling, advocacy, medical, and legal resources Issuing a “No Contact Order” Explaining your rights and resources for reporting sexual assault to law enforcement and/or College officials Requesting academic extensions or accommodations (such as assistance in transferring to another section of a course, assistance in requesting withdrawal or an incomplete grade in a particular course, leaves of absence or withdrawal from the College, or assistance requesting alternate methods of completing coursework) Assistance in relocating an on-campus housing assignment or campus job Increased security and monitoring of certain areas of the campus Arranging a meeting to discuss safety planning Providing step by step assistance with investigations under the Sexual Misconduct Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/) Providing financial aid-related information Transportation or parking accommodations Connecting you with a variety of other campus and community resources Students do not need to participate in an investigation or file charges in order to request support from the Office of Title IX.

(see https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/)

Please ensure all required documents are submitted by June 5. EOF Advisors are available for both in-person and virtual meetings. For general quest… (see https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/)

(see https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/freshman/)

How-to and policies: Purpose of EOF Program: The Educational Opportunity Fund \(EOF\) Program at Ramapo College of New Jersey provides meaningful access to higher education for qualified New Jersey students impacted by historical poverty. (see https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/eof-program/)

question: who is in charge of residence life
good_reply: Lisa Gonsisko, Director of the Office of Residence Life (named on the Behavioral Intervention Team page). Residence Life's own contacts may be added.
must_not: Saying no director is listed; naming a residence director or RA as the head. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

[2]

Behavioral Intervention Team: Dr. Judith Green is Director, Center for Student Wellness; Lisa Gonsisko is Director, Office of Residence Life; Jason Balsan is Director, Department of Public Safety; Dr. David C. - **Behavioral Intervention Team**: Phone: Chairperson (201) 684-7869. Email: bit@ramapo.edu. [12]

body.answer:
I can't see live updates, like the weather, closings or how busy a place is right now.

The Interim Dean of Undergraduate Studies and Honors is Mike Unger; his listed office is ASB 123 [14, 20]. I don’t have verified information about whether he is in today or whether his office accepts application drop-offs. Contact the Office of the Provost (ugstudies@ramapo.edu) [20] or the Ramapo Honors Program (honors@ramapo.edu) [6] to check.

Ramapo’s listed announcements cover college closings, not an individual dean’s availability: RCNJ Alerts, the Telephone Announcement Line at (201) 236-2902, and the College webpage provide closing information; during a complete College closing, a sign is placed by the Public Safety Booth at the campus main entrance [12].

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [21]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [21]

question: how do i start my own club
good_reply: Through the Student Government Association: the SGA Vice President explains how to start a club, and SGA's Club Process & Allocations Committee reviews the proposed constitution and the Archway application. Contact sga@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Only how to join an existing club. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
1. Student Government Association: The Club Process & Allocations Committee, chaired by the Vice President and with membership limited to SGA members & club/organization leaders, works with students who want to start new clubs on campus. [1]
2. Student Government Association: After the Vice President instructs the Committee on how to start a new club, it reviews the proposed constitution and Archway application. [1]
3. Center for Student Involvement: Browse the list; if your interests are not represented, inquire about starting a new club or organization. [4]
4. Center for Student Involvement: Once the College recognizes an organization, it is eligible to receive financial support from the Student Activities Allocations Committee. [4]
5. Center for Student Involvement: Student Government Association (SGA) ([https://www.ramapo.edu/sga/](https://www.ramapo.edu/sga/)) Listen WRPR-FM Online ([https://www.ramapo.edu/wrpr-fm/](https://www.ramapo.edu/wrpr-fm/)) [4]

- **Student Government Association**: Phone: (201) 684-7271. Email: sga@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-225. [11]
- **Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [11]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/sga/getting-involved/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/clubs/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is a Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. It focuses on how governmental laws and policies shape human lives, and trains students in research methodologies, quantitative and qualitative methods, and skills for work with or for public institutions. [1]

Requirements: Required Courses—all of PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; and PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP. Electives—Select 3, at least 3 of: ACCT 502 GOVERNMENT AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ACCOUNTING; ACCT 625 INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING; BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS; BADM 503 BUSINESS LAW, ETHICS & REGULATORY PRONOUNCEMENTS; DATA 601 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE; DATA 670 DATA VISUALIZATION; MATH 570 APPLIED STATISTICS; MATH 685 INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; MBAD 610 BECOMING A 21ST CENTURY LEADER; MBAD 625 CRISIS & CHANGE MANAGEMENT; NURS 660 LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION IN HEALTHCARE; NURS 670 HEALTHCARE ECONOMICS AND FINANCE; NURS 808 HEALTH POLICY LEADERSHIP; MSWK 505 SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS AND POLICIES I; MSWK 507 CULTURAL DIVERSITY, RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; MSWK 604 ADVANCED SOCIAL POLICY; MSWK 610 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; MSWK 670 SOCIAL WELFARE POLICIES IN HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH. [1]

Also published: Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor. [1]

Graduate Admissions lists one professional or academic letter of recommendation; applicants enter references’ names and contact information in the online application’s ‘Recommendations’ section, and Ramapo sends the request for references to upload recommendations to the application portal. The letter is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent Ramapo graduates from 2025 and 2026. Also required: a 400-word personal statement describing why you are interested in the program, how it fits into personal intellectual development and what you expect to accomplish by enrolling, and a resume. [6] Details: [https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/)

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Nursing RN to BSN is a track in Ramapo’s Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program for registered nurses with an Associate’s degree or Diploma in nursing. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Ramapo’s Nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). Diploma nursing graduates are granted 30 credits for their diploma nursing courses upon satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1]

Requirements:
- Required Math Course — Select 1: MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; or SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY.
- RN to BSN Professional Core — Required Courses all of: NURS 312 NURSING INFORMATICS; NURS 316 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; NURS 330 HEALTH ASSESSMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; and NURS 460 CLINICAL MANAGEMENT.
- Elective — Select 1. Students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Also published: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [17]:
- Friday, October 16, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade)

Registrar: If you complete the work by the completion date on the Incomplete Form or the academic calendar (the earliest date will be honored), the assigned grade replaces the I. If you do not satisfactorily complete it by then, the grade changes to F. [4] Review the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for Incomplete Deadlines; the Incomplete Form must be completed by you and the instructor. [4] Submit it to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu). [4] The Incomplete Request Form must be received by the Office of the Registrar by the last day of the semester/session. [4]

In extraordinary circumstances, you may request an incomplete extension. [6] It may only be extended until the end of the semester following the semester the incomplete grade was given. [6] Obtain the incomplete extension form from the Office of the Registrar; it requires your signature and faculty approval. [6] Submit it by the last day to resolve an incomplete grade posted on the Academic Calendar. [6] Extension of an Incomplete Form ([https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Extension-of-an-Incomplete-Form-FILLABLE.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Extension-of-an-Incomplete-Form-FILLABLE.pdf)) [8]

Office of the Provost: I; Incomplete Given in extenuating circumstances (for instance, reasons of illness or other emergency) when approved by the instructor and when requested by a student who has satisfactorily completed at least two-thirds of course requirements prior to the end of a term on an Incomplete Request form. [13] The default deadline for completion of course work is posted on the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for each semester (typically February 26 for fall semester incompletes and October 15 for spring and summer incompletes, or the next business day); however, the instructor may set an earlier deadline at the time the Incomplete grade is requested. [13] When work is completed before the deadline, the instructor completes a Grade Adjustment Request form and the new assigned grade replaces the I. If work is not satisfactorily completed by the deadline, the grade changes to F. A student may not graduate with an I grade outstanding. [13]

facts.says: If the work is completed by the completion date indicated on the Incomplete Form or the academic calendar (the earliest date will be honored), the grade assigned replaces the I. If the work is not satisfactorily completed by the completion date the grade is changed to F. Requesting an Incomplete Grade: Review the Academic Calendar (https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) for Incomplete Deadlines The Incomplete Form must be completed by the student and the instructor.
The form must be submitted to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu).
The Incomplete Request Form must be received in the Office of the Registrar by the last day of the semester/session.
In extraordinary circumstances a student may request an incomplete extension.
The incomplete may only be extended until the end of the semester following the semester the incomplete grade was given.
The incomplete extension form must be obtained from the Office of the Registrar and requires the student’s signature and the faculty’s approval.

I; Incomplete Given in extenuating circumstances (for instance, reasons of illness or other emergency) when approved by the instructor and when requested by a student who has satisfactorily completed at least two-thirds of course requirements prior to the end of a term on an Incomplete Request form.

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Office of the Provost: Credit load limits for graduate students are defined by the individual graduate program [1]. In Fall and Spring, a matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit [2]. If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor before making the request to the Office of the Registrar [2]. If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean [2]. All matriculated undergraduate students should consult with the Office of Financial Aid before changing or exceeding credit load limits [2]. Each graduate program director will recommend to the Dean of the school that houses the program the maximum number of credits per semester or cohort term, and it will be posted to program’s Catalog page [4]. The Dean will communicate that decision to the Registrar [4].

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester [7]. A student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload [7]. The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload [7]. The credit overload request form can be found here ([https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/)) [7].

Registrar: The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student wishes to take more than the maximum for their program [10]. A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above [10]. Credit overloads will incur additional charges [10].

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [16]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [16]

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

**Office of the Provost**
Under some limited circumstances, a student may appeal a grade. Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case. Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy. Appeals that will not be considered include, but are not limited to, those based on a student’s perceived need for a higher grade (for instance, in order to raise their GPA or to enable the course to transfer to another institution) and those based on grades that were penalized (for example, a sanction of a 0 on an assignment or an F in the course) because the student was found responsible for violating the Academic Integrity Policy. [2]
If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter. Supporting documentation must be provided. Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion. Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade. If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor. The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate. If the Dean determines that a grade change is warranted, the Dean will forward an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request with explanatory reasons to the Registrar and advise the course instructor and student in writing. facts.says: Under some limited circumstances, a student may appeal a grade.
Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case.

Appeals that will not be considered include, but are not limited to, those based on a student’s perceived need for a higher grade (for instance, in order to raise their GPA or to enable the course to transfer to another institution) and those based on grades that were penalized (for example, a sanction of a 0 on an assignment or an F in the course) because the student was found responsible for violating the Academic Integrity Policy.

If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter.
Supporting documentation must be provided.
Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion.
Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade.

If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor.

If the Dean determines that a grade change is warranted, the Dean will forward an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request with explanatory reasons to the Registrar and advise the course instructor and student in writing.
If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email.

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Financial Aid:
- If you drop below full-time status, your financial aid will be adjusted. [1]
- Federal aid requires you to be enrolled in 6 credits in a semester. [1]
- If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits, your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans. [1]
- If you have state aid, it may be canceled; institutional grants and scholarships could also be reduced or taken away. [1]
- Federal aid should not be affected if you are still enrolled for 6 or more credits. [2]
- NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires that students be enrolled full time at the time the aid is fully disbursed to your account. [2]
- If you drop below full-time status, which is less than 12 credits, your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester. [3]
- Please contact the Office of Financial Aid to discuss your situation before making a change that drops you below full-time status for the semester. [3]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [12]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

pageFacts.question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid

facts.says: If you drop below full-time status your financial aid will be adjusted.
Federal aid requires you to be enrolled in 6 credits in a semester.
If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans.
If you have state aid that is subject to being canceled and institutional grants and scholarships could also be reduced or taken away.
Federal aid should not be affected if a student is still enrolled for 6 or more credits.
NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires that students be enrolled full time at the time the aid is fully disbursed to your account.
If you drop below full-time status which is less than 12 credits your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester.
Please contact the Office of Financial Aid to discuss your situation before making a change that drops you below full-time status for the semester.

question: can i still add a class this semester
good_reply: No: the last day to add full-semester fall courses was Sep 1, 2026 (Session II: Oct 21). Winter classes start Dec 17 and Spring 2027 registration is open (since Oct 27).
must_not: Telling the student they can still add; leaving out that the deadline passed.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [11]:
- Friday, August 28, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Tuesday, September 1, 2026: Full Semester Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Thursday, December 17, 2026: Last Day to Add/Drop Winter Classes with 100% Tuition Refund (also on the Winter 2027 calendar)

No. Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): You can add or drop courses before or within the first week of classes each semester [1]. Registrar: In general, you can adjust your schedule anytime after your day to register arrives through the last day of Add/Drop [2]. question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

Housing & Residence Life
1. Register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS) if you are requesting specific housing accommodations due to a medically related condition. [1]
2. Submit your request no later than published deadlines. [1]

Office of Specialized Services
3. First register for affiliation with OSS to request a housing accommodation based on a disability. [3]
4. Initiate contact with OSS to receive services or arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [3]
5. Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations and/or adjustments. [3]
6. For only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor, you do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms. [3]
7. For those requests, complete only a request for disability support form. [3]
8. See “How To Request OSS Services” ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/)) for more information. [3]
9. Expect a decision within twenty one (21) business days after OSS receives all requested documentation. [4]
10. If the information is insufficient for OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee to determine whether an accommodation is necessary, OSS will inform you in writing that more information is needed and may request to speak directly with the professional supplying it. [4]
11. Refer to the Office of Specializes Services (OSS) Housing Accommodation Request Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf)) for a comprehensive description of how to request a housing accommodation. [5]
12. To assist a student with specific housing needs, the student must affiliate with OSS by providing documentation verifying a disability and the need for the requested accommodation. [6]
13. OSS staff and, in most cases, the Housing Accommodation Request Committee review the request. [6]
14. Once approved, OSS works with Residence Life on appropriate placement. [https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [6]

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [13]
- **Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/apply/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/frequently-asked-questions/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

facts.says: Any resident, who is requesting specific housing accommodations, due to a medically related condition, will need to register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Please submit requests for housing accommodations no later than published deadlines.
All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Check out our webpage “How To Request OSS Services” (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/) for more information.
Students must initiate contact with OSS in order to receive services or to arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments.

Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted in order to establish eligibility and to determine which accommodations and/or adjustments are appropriate for each student.

Note: Students requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms, as below.
Students only need to complete a request for disability support form.
Students can expect a decision about their request within twenty one (21) business days of OSS receiving all requested documentation.

If the information provided does not contain sufficient information for OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee to determine whether an accommodation is necessary, OSS will inform the individual in writing that more information is needed and may request to speak directly with the professional supplying that information.

For a comprehensive description on how to request a housing accommodation please refer to the Office of Specializes Services (OSS) Housing Accommodation Request Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf).

A: In order to assist a student who has specific housing needs, the student must affiliate with OSS by providing documentation verifying the presence of a disability and the need for the requested accommodation.
The request is then reviewed by the OSS staff and in most cases the Housing Accommodation Request Committee.

Once approved, OSS will work with Residence Life on having the student appropriately placed.https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/ Q: How can I be placed in a residence hall that has a kitchen?

question: i broke my wrist and cant write for a few weeks. can OSS help me with notes and exams
good_reply: Yes, OSS serves students with temporary disabilities such as a broken limb: submit the Application for Disability Support and current documentation, then an intake meeting with the OSS Director or Assistant Director authorizes accommodations. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Saying OSS only helps permanent disabilities. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

Office of Specialized Services: Yes. Log into OSSOnline to review your courses and select semester accommodations. [2] It’s a good idea to contact your OSS Counselor with questions. [2] After you select accommodations in OSSOnline, your Counselor is notified to review and approve them. [2] It’s best to request accommodations the week prior to the start of classes. [2] Your Counselor will e-mail you and your Instructors copies of your Accommodation Notice; after the initial notice, you can print extra copies in OSSOnline. [2] For notetaker questions or concerns, contact your OSS Counselor. [3] Schedule a meeting on Connect with your OSS Counselor and request a notetaker to review semester accommodations. [4] For help, email Alternative Testing staff at osstests@ramapo.edu; faculty receive an electronic copy of student accommodations, including the Faculty Alternative Testing Agreement link. [5] Submit exam reservations through OSSOnline no later than 7 days before scheduled on campus exams and 14 days before on campus final exams. [5] Impairments may cause unpredictable, prolonged absences; interfere with physical skills for lab, computer or writing assignments; make writing difficult due to arthritis pain or joint deformities; hinder people with Multiple Sclerosis from handling small lab equipment or precise measuring, graphing or drawing; make prolonged sitting challenging with chronic pain or back problems; limit mobility after illness or injury, requiring a wheelchair or scooter; or require avoiding activities that trigger a condition. [6] Potential accommodations include notetakers or scribes, audio-recording classes, flexible attendance, short-term assignment extensions when possible, extended testing time or alternative testing, electronic assignments and course materials, speech-recognition input devices, and mobility accommodations when health conditions cause mobility problems. [6] Peer Notetaking must be approved during the affiliation process. [7] If supported and approved by the OSS Director, it will be listed on your Accommodation Notice. [7] Once approved, you still need to request notetakers each semester. [7]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [13]

This office can help:
**Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [14]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/alternative-testing-for-students/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/notetaking/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/notetaking/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/alternative-testing-for-students/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/disabilities-and-teaching-strategies-accommodations/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/notetaking/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

It’s a good idea to be in touch with your OSS Counselor, and definitely contact them if you have any questions!

Your Counselor will e-mail you and your Instructors copies of your Accommodation Notice (FYI: after the initial notice is sent, you can log into OSSOnline and print out extra copies of the Accommodation Notice yourself!)

Potential Accommodations / Teaching Strategies: Notetakers or scribes Audio-recording of classes Flexible attendance policy Short-term extensions on assignments when possible Extended testing time or alternative testing arrangements Assignments available in electronic format Electronic distribution of course materials Speech recognition computer input devices When health conditions result in mobility problems, accommodations for students with mobility impairments may be appropriate.

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends. Office of Specialized Services: Please call our office at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest in having an Emotional Support Animal on campus. [1] Interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director to discuss further. [1] A student with a disability must register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS), provide disability documentation demonstrating the benefits provided by the emotional support animal, and be granted an accommodation permitting the animal on campus. [2] Use of emotional support animals may be limited to defined areas of campus and generally will not be permitted in academic or recreational facilities. [2] The College is committed to accommodate students and others with disabilities who require service or support animals. [3] Animals are allowed on campus only when providing service or support to a member of the College or guest to campus as a reasonable disability accommodation. [3] This policy applies to individuals with disabilities accompanied by a service animal or requiring a support animal while on campus. [3] OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a requested accommodation if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented. [4] OSS together with the Housing Accommodation Request Committee shall determine if the requested accommodation is reasonable. [4] An accommodation may be deemed unreasonable if: 1) the student’s documented condition does not rise to the level of a disability; 2) documentation does not provide adequate evidence to support the request; 3) it imposes an undue financial and or administrative burden on the college; 4) it fundamentally alters college housing policy; 5) it poses a direct threat to the health and safety of others or would cause substantial property damage to the property of others, including college property. [4] For an emotional support animal request, if applicable, the College may also inquire as to the age, size/breed of the animal to determine whether the accommodation is reasonable. [4] All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS). [5] Students must initiate contact with OSS to receive services or arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [5] Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations and/or adjustments for each student. [5]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [16]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

How to Appeal Your Parking Citation Click Here to Go to the Appeal Portal ([https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3)) Appeals are input online via the form An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the issuance of a citation. Failure to file the appeal within twenty (20) days constitutes forfeiture of the right to appeal. [1]
Appeals will not be considered for: Ignorance of the regulation Stated inability to find a legal parking space Operation of the vehicle by another person Stated failure of parking enforcement staff to ticket previously for similar offenses Inability to pay the fine Disagreement with Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations Citations issued by the Mahwah Police Department Appellants must identify upon which specific ground(s) they are appealing and briefly describe their justification. [2]
During regular business hours, payments may be made to the Office of Student Accounts. You must FIRST stop at the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, or contact parking services at parking@ramapo.edu (mailto:parking@ramapo.edu), to ensure that the fine has been transferred to your student account. IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS: Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee. The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days. A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [3]

Select Payment Method Once processed your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid. [4]

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts:
1. Run an On-Demand Statement to view current, real-time account activity and balances. View the eBill statement to designate a third-party (i.e. parents) as Authorized Users to view the bill and make payments. This is the only place to make an online payment, such as by credit/debit card or ACH; you can enroll in a monthly payment plan and access all previous bills. [1]
2. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)). Locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab at the top of the page. Select the term you wish to pay for and click Continue. From the Payment Method drop down, select Credit Card via PayPath, then click Select. Verify or modify the payment amount, then click Continue to PayPath. Read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer on the Welcome to the PayPath Payment Service! [6]
3. On the Screen, click Continue. Review the payment amount information and click Continue. Enter all Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click Continue. The data you entered, including the service fee amount charged by PayPath, will be displayed. [6]
4. The credit/debit card service fee is based on a rate of 3.0% with a minimum fee of $3.00. [6]
5. Review your entries. If any data is incorrect, click Change Information. If you do not wish to have your transaction processed, click Cancel. Click Submit to submit your payment. By submitting your entry, you accept the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]
6. Verify your bank account routing and account number before submitting your payment. [8]
7. These payments can ONLY be made ON-LINE. [8]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

facts.says: to view current, real-time account activity and balances, running an On-Demand Statement and viewing the eBill statement the place to designate a third-party (i.e. parents) to view the bill and make payments as Authorized Users the only place to make an online payment, such as a credit/debit card or ACH payment where you can enroll in a monthly payment plan where you can access all of your previous bills

Screen, then click on the Continue button Review payment amount information then click the Continue button Enter all Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click on Continue button All of the data you entered will be displayed, including the service fee amount charged by PayPath.

to verify your bank account routing and account number before submitting your payment.

question: Who is the Title IX coordinator at Ramapo, and which office are they in?
good_reply: Kat McGee, J.D., Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance (the Title IX Coordinator): Office D 104, (201) 684-7220, kmcgee@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Leaving out the office when asked. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
I'm sorry that happened. You deserve to feel safe. If you're in danger right now, call 911.

Title IX phone: (201) 684-7220. [1] Title IX is in D-104. [1] Title IX: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance: kmcgee@ramapo.edu To file a complaint at the College about an incident of discrimination and/or sexual misconduct: titleix@ramapo.edu [1]

Title IX's page "Who is the College’s Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator?" says: "Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)" [2]

Title IX's page "What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?" says: "The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. This includes management of grievances, investigations, and the disposition of complaints of sexual harassment, violence, rape, and discrimination under the Sexual Misconduct Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/titleix/sexual-misconduct-policy/))." (more on its page) [2]

good_reply: You Can Narcan! on Mon Nov 16 at 6 PM (College Park Apartments).
must_not: Saying nothing is listed. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is a Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. It focuses on how government laws and policies shape lives, and trains students in research methodologies, quantitative and qualitative methods, and skills for working with or for public institutions. [1]

Requirements: Take all of PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; and PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP. Select 3 electives, at least 3, from: ACCT 502 GOVERNMENT AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ACCOUNTING; ACCT 625 INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING; BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS; BADM 503 BUSINESS LAW, ETHICS & REGULATORY PRONOUNCEMENTS; DATA 601 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE; DATA 670 DATA VISUALIZATION; MATH 570 APPLIED STATISTICS; MATH 685 INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; MBAD 610 BECOMING A 21ST CENTURY LEADER; MBAD 625 CRISIS & CHANGE MANAGEMENT; NURS 660 LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION IN HEALTHCARE; NURS 670 HEALTHCARE ECONOMICS AND FINANCE; NURS 808 HEALTH POLICY LEADERSHIP; MSWK 505 SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS AND POLICIES I; MSWK 507 CULTURAL DIVERSITY, RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; MSWK 604 ADVANCED SOCIAL POLICY; MSWK 610 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; MSWK 670 SOCIAL WELFARE POLICIES IN HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH. [1]

Also published: Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor. [1]

Graduate Admissions lists a professional or academic letter of recommendation. Enter references’ names and contact information in the online application’s “Recommendations” section; Ramapo sends an automated request and references upload recommendations to the application portal. The letter is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent Ramapo graduates from 2025 and 2026. The listed materials also include a 400-word personal statement describing your interest, fit with personal intellectual development, and expected accomplishments, and a resume. [6]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing program for registered nurses prepared at the Associate’s degree or Diploma level. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Ramapo says it has articulation agreements with Bergen Community College, County College of Morris and Rockland. The nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). Diploma-program graduates are granted 30 credits for diploma nursing courses upon satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1]

Requirements:
• Required Math Course — select 1: MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; or SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY.
• RN to BSN Professional Core — all of: NURS 312 NURSING INFORMATICS; NURS 316 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; NURS 330 HEALTH ASSESSMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; NURS 460 CLINICAL MANAGEMENT.
• Elective — select 1. Students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

The catalog also lists Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN and Nursing MSN. [1]

Catalog: [https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS) [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor (Minor) consists of five courses (20 credits). [1] The requirements are: [1]
- Required: BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY.
- Select 1 Statistics or Research Methods course: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS; MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS.
- Select 1 Health Policy and Management course: COMM 383 THEORY AND PRACTICE OF HEALTH COMMUNICATION; ECON 332 HEALTH ECONOMICS: AN INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE; ENST 317 ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY AND REGULATION; MGMT 330 HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATION; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; or PUBL 201 PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC POLICY.
- Select 1 Social and Behavioral Science course: SCIN 310 AIDS: BIOLOGICAL, MEDICAL, SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SWRK 230 AIDS: SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SWRK 328 COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH; PHLT 305 HEALTH AND WELLNESS; or PHLT 390 TOPICS.
- Select 1 Global or Population Health course: ANTH 307 MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY; NURS 220 COMMUNITY HEALTH AND TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE; NURS 365 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; PHLT 290 TOPICS; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; or SPAN 311 SPANISH FOR HEALTH CARE AND HUMAN SERVICES PROFESSIONALS. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-PHLT)

question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [16]:
- Friday, October 16, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, December 15, 2026: Full and Session II Courses - Last Day to Request an Incomplete ("I" Grade)

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): If the work is not satisfactorily completed by the deadline, the grade changes to F; completed work replaces the I. [1]

Registrar: The Incomplete Form and academic calendar give completion dates; the earlier date applies. [3] The student and instructor must complete the Incomplete Form. [3] The Incomplete Request Form must reach the Office of the Registrar by the last day of the semester/session. [3] Submit the form to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu). [3]

1. In extraordinary circumstances, you may request an incomplete extension. [5] It can extend only until the end of the semester following the semester the I was given. [5] Obtain the extension form from the Office of the Registrar; it needs the student’s signature and faculty approval. [5] Submit it to the Office of the Registrar by the last day to resolve an incomplete on the Academic Calendar. [5]
2. In extraordinary circumstances, you may petition for an incomplete extension. [10] Get the extension form from the Office of the Registrar. [10] File it with the Office of the Registrar no later than the last day to resolve an incomplete on the Academic Calendar. [10]

Office of the Provost: An I is for extenuating circumstances, such as illness or another emergency, when the instructor approves and the student has completed at least two-thirds of course requirements before the term ends, using an Incomplete Request form. [13] The default course-work deadline is on the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for each semester (typically February 26 for fall semester incompletes and October 15 for spring and summer incompletes, or the next business day); the instructor may set an earlier deadline when the I is requested. [13] If work is completed before the deadline, the instructor submits a Grade Adjustment Request form and the new grade replaces the I. If it is not satisfactorily completed by the deadline, the grade becomes F. A student may not graduate with an I outstanding. [13]

question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
18 credits: Office of the Provost says a matriculated student wishing to register for more than 18 credits per semester in Fall and Spring, at additional cost, must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit. [2] If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, they must get approval from their academic advisor before making the request to the Office of the Registrar. [2] More than 20 credits requires approval from the student’s school Dean. [2] All matriculated undergraduate students should consult with the Office of Financial Aid before changing or exceeding credit load limits. [2] In Winter, students may register for a maximum of one course or 4 credits. [2]

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester, but can request more by applying for a credit overload. [7] The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the overload. [7] The credit overload request form is at [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/). [7]

Registrar: The credit overload request form is for an undergraduate student wishing to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student wishing to take more than the maximum for their program. [10] A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above. [10] Full policy details are at the Credit Overload Policy: [https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-load1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-load1). [10] Credit overloads will incur additional charges. [10]

If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean.
All matriculated undergraduate students should consult with the Office of Financial Aid before changing or exceeding credit load limits.
Winter Students may register for a maximum of one course or 4 credits in the Winter session.
A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester.
However, a student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload.
The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload.
The credit overload request form can be found here (https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/).
The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program.
A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above.

facts.says: Fall and Spring A matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit.
If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar.
If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean.
All matriculated undergraduate students should consult with the Office of Financial Aid before changing or exceeding credit load limits.
Winter Students may register for a maximum of one course or 4 credits in the Winter session.
A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester.
However, a student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload.
The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload.
The credit overload request form can be found here (https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/).
The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program.
A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above.
Full policy details can be found by visiting the Credit Overload Policy (https://catalog.ramapo.edu/quicklinks/academicpolicies#credit-load1).
Credit overloads will incur additional charges. Δ

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

**Office of the Provost**
Under some limited circumstances, a student may appeal a grade. Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case. Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy. Appeals that will not be considered include, but are not limited to, those based on a student’s perceived need for a higher grade (for instance, in order to raise their GPA or to enable the course to transfer to another institution) and those based on grades that were penalized (for example, a sanction of a 0 on an assignment or an F in the course) because the student was found responsible for violating the Academic Integrity Policy. [2]
If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter. Supporting documentation must be provided. Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion. Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade. If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor. The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate. If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email. The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination. If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost. The petition is initiated by the submission of a written statement by the student, submitted by email or certified letter, that explains their position and includes any evidence that contradicts the Dean’s decision or contains information that had heretofore been unavailable. [3]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [21]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [22]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

pageFacts.question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline

facts.says: Under some limited circumstances, a student may appeal a grade.
Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case.

Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy.

Appeals that will not be considered include, but are not limited to, those based on a student’s perceived need for a higher grade (for instance, in order to raise their GPA or to enable the course to transfer to another institution) and those based on grades that were penalized (for example, a sanction of a 0 on an assignment or an F in the course) because the student was found responsible for violating the Academic Integrity Policy.

If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter.
Supporting documentation must be provided.
Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion.
Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade.

If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor.

The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate.
If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email.
The Deans have 15 calendar days to make this determination.
If the Dean renders an opinion which does not support the student’s grade appeal, the student may petition for a review by the Office of the Provost.

The petition is initiated by the submission of a written statement by the student, submitted by email or certified letter, that explains their position and includes any evidence that contradicts the Dean’s decision or contains information that had heretofore been unavailable.

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Financial Aid:
If you drop below full-time status your financial aid will be adjusted. [1]
Federal aid requires you to be enrolled in 6 credits in a semester. [1]
If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans. [1]
If you have state aid that is subject to being canceled, institutional grants and scholarships could also be reduced or taken away. [1]
Federal aid should not be affected if a student is still enrolled for 6 or more credits. [2]
NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires that students be enrolled full time at the time the aid is fully disbursed to your account. [2]
If you drop below full-time status which is less than 12 credits your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester. [3]
Please contact the Office of Financial Aid to discuss your situation before making a change that drops you below full-time status for the semester. [3]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [12]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can i still add a class this semester
good_reply: No: the last day to add full-semester fall courses was Sep 1, 2026 (Session II: Oct 21). Winter classes start Dec 17 and Spring 2027 registration is open (since Oct 27).
must_not: Telling the student they can still add; leaving out that the deadline passed.

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [11]:
- Friday, August 28, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Tuesday, September 1, 2026: Full Semester Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Thursday, December 17, 2026: Last Day to Add/Drop Winter Classes with 100% Tuition Refund (also on the Winter 2027 calendar)

It depends. Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): You can add or drop courses before or within the first week of classes each semester [1]. After the add/drop period ends, you can no longer add classes to your schedule [1]. For deadlines regarding add/drop, withdraw, or incomplete, please refer to the academic calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) [1]. Registrar: In general, you can adjust your schedule anytime after your day to register arrives through the last day of Add/Drop [2]. Students are eligible to add a course to their student schedule once registration for a given term has opened [3]. Please consult the academic calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for important dates [3]. Spring: application available October 15 to April 1; deadline April 1; official conferral June 17, 2027; diploma mailed Late July; commencement ceremony To Be Announced. Summer: application available March 1 to May 31*; deadline May 31*; official conferral August 21, 2026; diploma mailed Late September; commencement ceremony To Be Announced. *Graduation Applications received after April 1 will not be listed in the Commencement Program.
