question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

Housing & Residence Life
1. Register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS) if you are requesting specific housing accommodations due to a medically related condition. [1]
2. Once affiliated, OSS will inform the Office of Residence Life about residents who need specific housing accommodations based on medical documentation provided to OSS. [1]
3. Submit housing accommodation requests no later than published deadlines. [1]

Office of Specialized Services

question: i broke my wrist and cant write for a few weeks. can OSS help me with notes and exams
good_reply: Yes, OSS serves students with temporary disabilities such as a broken limb: submit the Application for Disability Support and current documentation, then an intake meeting with the OSS Director or Assistant Director authorizes accommodations. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Saying OSS only helps permanent disabilities. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

Office of Specialized Services

1. Schedule a meeting on Connect with your OSS Counselor and request a notetaker during the meeting to review your accommodations for the semester. [4]

- Potential accommodations and teaching strategies include notetakers or scribes, audio-recording classes, flexible attendance, short-term assignment extensions when possible, extended testing time or alternative testing arrangements, electronic-format assignments, electronic course materials, speech-recognition computer input devices, and appropriate accommodations for mobility impairments when health conditions cause mobility problems. [5]

2. Log into OSSOnline to review your courses and select your accommodations for the semester. [6]
- It’s a good idea to be in touch with your OSS Counselor, and definitely contact them if you have questions. [6]
3. After you select your accommodations in OSSOnline, your OSS Counselor is notified to review and approve them. [6]
- It’s best to request accommodations the week prior to the start of classes. [6]
- Your Counselor will e-mail you and your Instructors copies of your Accommodation Notice. After the initial notice is sent, you can log into OSSOnline and print extra copies yourself. [6]
- For in-person courses, proctoring assistance is available through OSS Alternative Testing staff, Monday to Friday. [7]
- Submit an exam reservation through OSSOnline no later than 7 days prior to the scheduled on campus exam and 14 days prior to the on campus final exam. [7]
- Peer Notetaking must be approved during the affiliation process. [8]
- If supported and approved by the OSS Director, this accommodation will be indicated on your Accommodation Notice. [8]
- Once approved, you will still need to request notetakers each semester. [8]
- The Office of Specialized Services provides information and support services to Ramapo College students with permanent and temporary disabilities. [9]
- Once incoming students have provided an Application for Disability Support and current disability verification to the OSS office, they will be scheduled for an individual intake appointment with the OSS Director or Assistant Director. [9]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [13]

This office can help:
**Health Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7536. Location: Near the campus South Gate entrance at the corner of Route 202 and Hornbeam Road. [14]

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
It depends. Office of Specialized Services: Please call our office at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest in having an Emotional Support Animal on campus. [1] Interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director to discuss further. [1] Please refer to the Emotional Support Animal Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/)) for more information. [1] A student must register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS), provide disability documentation demonstrating the benefits provided by the emotional support animal, and be granted an accommodation permitting the animal on campus. [2] Use of emotional support animals may be limited to defined areas of campus and generally will not be permitted in academic or recreational facilities. [2] For more information concerning emotional support animals of campus, please refer to the Emotional Support Animal Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/08/Emotional-Support-Animal-Policy-2022.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/08/Emotional-Support-Animal-Policy-2022.pdf)). [2] The College is committed to accommodating students and others with disabilities that require service or support animals. [3] Animals are only allowed on campus when providing service or support to a member of the College or guest to campus as a reasonable disability accommodation. [3] This policy applies to people with disabilities accompanied by a service animal or requiring a support animal on campus. [3] OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a requested accommodation if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented. [4] OSS together with the Housing Accommodation Request Committee shall determine if the requested accommodation is reasonable. [4] An accommodation may be unreasonable if: 1) the student’s documented condition does not rise to the level of a disability; 2) documentation does not provide adequate evidence to support the request; 3) it imposes an undue financial and or administrative burden on the college; 4) it fundamentally alters college housing policy; 5) it poses a direct threat to the health and safety of others or would cause substantial property damage to the property of others, including college property. [4] Regarding an emotional support animal request, if applicable the College may also inquire about the animal’s age, size/breed to determine whether the accommodation is reasonable. [4] All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS). [5]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [16]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

pageFacts.question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work

facts.says: Please call our office at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest in having an Emotional Support Animal on campus.
Interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director to discuss further.
Please refer to the Emotional Support Animal Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) for more information.

When a student with a disability has registered with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS), provided disability documentation demonstrating the benefits provided by the emotional support animal, and been granted an accommodation permitting the presence of the emotional support animal on campus.
Student use of emotional support animals may be limited to defined areas of campus and generally will not be permitted in academic or recreational facilities.

For more information concerning emotional support animals of campus, please refer to the Emotional Support Animal Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2022/08/Emotional-Support-Animal-Policy-2022.pdf).
However, the College is also committed to accommodate students and others with disabilities that require the assistance of service or support animals.
Animals are only allowed on campus when they are providing service or support to a member of the College or guest to campus as a reasonable disability accommodation.
This policy applies to those individuals with disabilities who will be accompanied by a service animal or who will require a support animal while on campus.
OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a requested accommodation if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented.
OSS together with the Housing Accommodation Request Committee shall determine if the requested accommodation is reasonable.

An accommodation may be deemed unreasonable if: 1) the student’s documented condition does not rise to the level of a disability; 2) documentation does not provide adequate evidence to support the request; 3) imposes an undue financial and or administrative burden on the college; 4) fundamentally alters college housing policy; 5) poses a direct threat to the health and safety of others or would cause substantial property damage to the property of others, including college property.
Regarding a request for an emotional support animal, if applicable the College may also inquire as to the age, size/breed of an animal in order to determine the reasonableness of this accommodation.
All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Public Safety: An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the issuance of a citation using the appeal portal: [https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3). [1] Failure to file within twenty (20) days forfeits the right to appeal. [2] Appeals will not be considered for ignorance of the regulation, stated inability to find a legal parking space, operation of the vehicle by another person, stated failure of parking enforcement staff to ticket previously for similar offenses, inability to pay the fine, or disagreement with Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations. The decision of the Appeals Board is FINAL. [1] Citations issued by the Mahwah Police Department will not be considered; appellants must identify the specific ground(s) for appeal and briefly describe their justification. [2]

During regular business hours, payments may be made to the Office of Student Accounts. [3] You must FIRST stop at the Parking and ID Office, Rm. C101, or contact parking services at parking@ramapo.edu, to ensure the fine has been transferred to your student account. [3] Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee. [3] The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days. [3] A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [3]

Citations are paid online using the payment portal: [https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). [4]
1. Enter Citation # and Fine Amount. [4]
2. Search for Citation. [4]
3. Select your Citation and follow the field required. [4]
4. Select Payment Method. Once processed your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid. [4]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [13]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts: To view current, real-time account activity and balances, run an On-Demand Statement and view the eBill statement. Use the eBill statement to designate a third-party (i.e. parents) to view the bill and make payments as Authorized Users; it is the only place to make online payments, such as credit/debit card or ACH payments, enroll in a monthly payment plan, and access previous bills. [1]

1. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)). Locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then click the Make Payment tab at the top of the page. Select the term you wish to make payment for and click Continue. [6]
2. From the Payment Method drop down, select Credit Card via PayPath, then click Select. Verify or modify the payment amount, then click Continue to PayPath. Read the non-refundable PayPath service fee disclaimer on the Welcome to the PayPath Payment Service! Screen, then click Continue. [6]
3. Review the payment amount information and click Continue. Enter all Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click Continue. All entered data, including the service fee amount charged by PayPath, will be displayed. [6]
4. The credit/debit card service fee is based on a rate of 3.0% with a minimum fee of $3.00. [6]
5. Verify your bank account routing and account number before submitting your payment. [7]
6. Review your entries. If any data is incorrect, click Change Information. To cancel the transaction, click Cancel. Click Submit to submit your payment; submitting accepts the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page for your records. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]
7. ACH payments are not accepted by phone or in-person; these payments can ONLY be made ON-LINE. [7]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: Who is the Title IX coordinator at Ramapo, and which office are they in?
good_reply: Kat McGee, J.D., Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance (the Title IX Coordinator): Office D 104, (201) 684-7220, kmcgee@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Leaving out the office when asked. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Title IX phone: (201) 684-7220. [1] Title IX is in D-104. [1] Title IX: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance: kmcgee@ramapo.edu To file a complaint at the College about an incident of discrimination and/or sexual misconduct: titleix@ramapo.edu [1]

Title IX's page "Who is the College’s Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator?" says: "Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)" [2]

(more on its page) [2]

value.text: Kat McGee, J.D. Director of Title IX and Institutional Compliance Office: D 104 (201) 684-7220 kmcgee@ramapo.edu (mailto:kmcgee@ramapo.edu)

value.heading: What does the Director of Title IX/Title IX Coordinator do?
value.text: The Director of Title IX is responsible for ensuring effective and timely responses to complaints of sexual violence, misconduct, discrimination or harassment by implementing Title IX related policies, coordinating appropriate training and resources, and identifying ways to prevent future discrimination. body.answer:
I can't see live updates, like the weather, closings or how busy a place is right now.

I don’t have verified information about whether the dean is in today. Ramapo’s pages name Michael Unger as Interim Dean of Undergraduate Studies and Honors, but don’t say whether he is present today. Contact the Office of the Provost to check. [28]

The application instructions I found describe emailing materials, not dropping them off. For current Ramapo freshmen who just completed their first semester, the page says to email PDFs of the admission essay, one faculty recommendation, and a sample of work to eaugis@ramapo.edu with the subject “Honors Application”; the work must be a regular PDF attachment, not an embedded link. [10] The catalog instead says to send those materials to honors@ramapo.edu. [16] The pages differ on the email address.

Ramapo’s announcements described here concern college closings and emergencies, not whether an individual dean is in. They include RCNJ Alerts, the college website, and the telephone announcement line, (201) 236-2902; during a complete closing, a sign is placed by the Public Safety Booth. [22][23][24]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [32]

question: how do i start my own club
good_reply: Through the Student Government Association: the SGA Vice President explains how to start a club, and SGA's Club Process & Allocations Committee reviews the proposed constitution and the Archway application. Contact sga@ramapo.edu.
must_not: Only how to join an existing club. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
1. Student Government Association: The Club Process & Allocations Committee, chaired by the Vice President and with membership limited to SGA members and club/organization leaders, works with students who want to start new clubs on campus. [1]
2. Student Government Association: After the Vice President instructs the committee on how to start a new club, it reviews the proposed constitution and Archway application. [1]
3. Center for Student Involvement: If you browse through this list and find your interests are not represented, inquire at the Center for Student Involvement about starting a new club or organization. [4]
4. Center for Student Involvement: Once the College recognizes an organization, it is eligible to receive financial support from the Student Activities Allocations Committee. [4]
5. Center for Student Involvement: Student Government Association (SGA) ([https://www.ramapo.edu/sga/](https://www.ramapo.edu/sga/)) Listen WRPR-FM Online ([https://www.ramapo.edu/wrpr-fm/](https://www.ramapo.edu/wrpr-fm/)) [4]

- **Student Government Association**: Phone: (201) 684-7271. Email: sga@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-225. [11]
- **Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [11]

question: tell me about the MPP
good_reply: The Public Policy MPP (Master of Public Policy) in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work, from its catalog description. The Public Policy 4+1 may be added.
must_not: Saying there is no such program; describing another program.

body.answer:
The Public Policy MPP is the Master of Public Policy in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work. It focuses on how governmental laws and policies shape lives and prepares students in research methods and skills for work with or for public institutions. [1] The catalog also publishes Public Policy 4+1 and Public Policy Minor. [1]

Requirements: all seven courses—PUBL 600 THE POLITICS OF POLICYMAKING; PUBL 601 FEDERAL PUBLIC POLICY & GOVERNANCE; PUBL 602 STATE & LOCAL PUBLIC POLICY; PUBL 616 ECONOMETRICS AND ANALYSIS; PUBL 618 PUBLIC MANAGEMENT; PUBL 621 POLITICAL ECONOMY; PUBL 705 PUBLIC POLICY INTERNSHIP—and select 3 electives (at least 3) from: ACCT 502 GOVERNMENT AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT ACCOUNTING; ACCT 625 INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTING; BADM 501 DATA ANALYTICS; BADM 503 BUSINESS LAW, ETHICS & REGULATORY PRONOUNCEMENTS; DATA 601 INTRODUCTION TO DATA SCIENCE; DATA 670 DATA VISUALIZATION; MATH 570 APPLIED STATISTICS; MATH 685 INTRODUCTION TO EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN; MBAD 610 BECOMING A 21ST CENTURY LEADER; MBAD 625 CRISIS & CHANGE MANAGEMENT; NURS 660 LEADERSHIP AND INNOVATION IN HEALTHCARE; NURS 670 HEALTHCARE ECONOMICS AND FINANCE; NURS 808 HEALTH POLICY LEADERSHIP; MSWK 505 SOCIAL WELFARE PROGRAMS AND POLICIES I; MSWK 507 CULTURAL DIVERSITY, RACISM, OPPRESSION AND PRIVILEGE; MSWK 604 ADVANCED SOCIAL POLICY; MSWK 610 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; MSWK 670 SOCIAL WELFARE POLICIES IN HEALTH AND MENTAL HEALTH. [1]

Admissions requirements listed: one professional or academic letter of recommendation, entered in the online application’s “Recommendations” section; Ramapo sends the reference an automated request to upload it to the application portal. This letter is waived for current Ramapo students graduating in 2027 and recent Ramapo graduates from 2025 and 2026. Also required: a 400-word personal statement describing your interest, how the program fits your personal intellectual development, and what you expect to accomplish by enrolling; and a resume. [6]

**Graduate Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7270. Email: graduate@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [15]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MPP-PBPL) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/graduate/requirements/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what's the RN to BSN
good_reply: The Nursing RN to BSN track, for registered nurses with an associate's degree or diploma who return for the BSN; one of three BSN tracks (generic, accelerated, RN to BSN); accredited by ACEN.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Nursing RN to BSN is a Bachelor of Science in Nursing program designed for registered nurses with an Associate’s degree or Diploma in nursing. Students transfer credits from their initial nursing program and complete Ramapo’s general education and nursing requirements. Ramapo’s Nursing programs are accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN). [1]

Diploma-program graduates are granted 30 credits for diploma nursing courses upon satisfactory completion of their first two BSN nursing courses. [1]

Requirements: Required Math Course—select 1: MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS, PSYC 242 STATISTICS, or SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY. RN to BSN Professional Core—required courses all of: NURS 312 NURSING INFORMATICS; NURS 316 PATHOPHYSIOLOGY; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; NURS 330 HEALTH ASSESSMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; NURS 460 CLINICAL MANAGEMENT. Elective—select 1; students should consult their Nursing advisor for elective course options. [1]

Other published levels: Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing MSN. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS)

question: how many classes is the public health minor and which ones count
good_reply: Five courses: BIOL 204 Epidemiology, plus one each from statistics/research methods, health policy and management, social and behavioral science, and global or population health, with examples from each list.
must_not: Leaving out a course group. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The Public Health Minor consists of five courses (20 credits). [1]

Requirements: [1]
- BIOL 204 EPIDEMIOLOGY (required).
- One statistics or research methods course: BADM 225 MANAGEMENT STATISTICS; ENSC 345 RESEARCH DESIGN & STATISTICS; MATH 370 APPLIED STATISTICS; NURS 325 NURSING RESEARCH AND EVIDENCE BASED PRACTICE; PSYC 242 STATISTICS; PSYC 303 RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; or SWRK 307 SOCIAL WORK RESEARCH METHODS.
- One health policy and management course: COMM 383 THEORY AND PRACTICE OF HEALTH COMMUNICATION; ECON 332 HEALTH ECONOMICS: AN INTERNATIONAL PERSPECTIVE; ENST 317 ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY AND REGULATION; MGMT 330 HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATION; NURS 445 LEADERSHIP IN A GLOBAL WORLD; or PUBL 201 PRINCIPLES OF PUBLIC POLICY.
- One social and behavioral science course: SCIN 310 AIDS: BIOLOGICAL, MEDICAL, SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SWRK 230 AIDS: SOCIAL PERSPECTIVES; SWRK 328 COMMUNITY MENTAL HEALTH; PHLT 305 HEALTH AND WELLNESS; or PHLT 390 TOPICS.
- One global or population health course: ANTH 307 MEDICAL ANTHROPOLOGY; NURS 220 COMMUNITY HEALTH AND TRADITIONAL CHINESE MEDICINE; NURS 365 PUBLIC HEALTH IN WEST AFRICA; NURS 425 COMMUNITY CENTERED NURSING; PHLT 290 TOPICS; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; or SPAN 311 SPANISH FOR HEALTH CARE AND HUMAN SERVICES PROFESSIONALS.

BIOL 204 requires BIOL 111 FUNDAMENTALS OF BIOLOGY I LECTURE. [3]

question: what happens if i take an incomplete and don't finish the work in time? can i get more time
good_reply: An I needs the instructor's approval and at least two-thirds of the course done. Work not finished by the date on the academic calendar turns the I into an F. In extraordinary circumstances a student can request an extension, up to the end of the following semester, on the Registrar's form with the student's signature and the faculty member's approval, due by the last day to resolve incompletes (Feb 12, 2027 for fall incompletes).
must_not: Leaving out that it becomes an F, or that an extension exists. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:

Registrar:
1. If you complete the work by the completion date on the Incomplete Form or academic calendar, whichever is earlier, the assigned grade replaces the I; otherwise, it changes to F. To request an Incomplete, review the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)); you and your instructor must complete the Incomplete Form. [3]
2. The form must be submitted to the Office of the Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu (mailto:reg@ramapo.edu). [3]
3. The Incomplete Request Form must be received by the Office of the Registrar by the last day of the semester/session. [3]
4. In extraordinary circumstances, you may request an extension. [5]
5. The incomplete may only be extended until the end of the semester following the semester it was given. [5]

[13] The default deadline is posted on the Academic Calendar ([https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/)) for each semester (typically February 26 for fall semester incompletes and October 15 for spring and summer incompletes, or the next business day); the instructor may set an earlier deadline when the I is requested. question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it
good_reply: 18 credits a semester. More needs a credit overload request through the Registrar (form), at extra cost; the GPA rule is 3.0 (the catalog says a student under 3.0 needs the advisor's approval first), and over 20 credits needs the school dean's approval.
must_not: Leaving out how to go over the limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Office of the Provost: In Fall and Spring, a matriculated student who wants more than 18 credits per semester must request that the Office of the Registrar raise the credit limit; this has an additional cost. [2] If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, they must first get approval from their academic advisor. [2] More than 20 credits also requires approval from the school Dean. [2]

Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): Students are typically permitted up to 18 credits per semester. [7] They can request more through a credit overload application. [7] To be granted an overload, the student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior. [7] Form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/) [7]

Registrar: The form is for undergraduates requesting more than 18 credits, or graduate students requesting more than their program maximum. [10] An overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above. [10] Credit overloads incur additional charges. [10]

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [16]
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [16]

pageFacts.question: whats the max credits i can take in a semester and can i go over it

facts.says: Fall and Spring A matriculated student who wishes to register for more than 18 credits per semester (at additional cost) must request that the Office of the Registrar raise their credit limit.
If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar.
If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean.
A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester.
However, a student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload.
The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload.
The credit overload request form can be found here (https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/).
The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program.
A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above.
Credit overloads will incur additional charges. Δ

If the student has under a 3.0 cumulative GPA, that student must obtain approval to raise the credit limit from their academic advisor prior to making the request to the Office of the Registrar.
If the student is attempting to register for more than 20 credits, they must obtain approval from their school Dean.
A student is typically permitted to take up to 18 credits per semester.
However, a student can request to take more than the allotted 18 credits by applying for a credit overload.
The student must have above a 3.0 GPA or be a graduating senior to be granted the credit overload.
The credit overload request form can be found here (https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/credit-overload-request-form/).
The credit overload request form is used when an undergraduate student wishes to take more than 18 credits or a graduate student that wishes to take more than the maximum for their program.
A credit overload is ONLY granted if the student has a 3.0 GPA or above.
Credit overloads will incur additional charges. Δ

question: i think my final grade is wrong, how do i appeal it and is there a deadline
good_reply: Within 20 calendar days after grades post, appeal in writing (email or certified letter) to the instructor with documentation; they have 15 days to decide. If no agreement, a written appeal to the dean of the school that sponsored the course within 20 days (15 days to decide), then a petition to the Office of the Provost within 20 days. Valid grounds: computational error, work not graded, a College policy violation (not wanting a higher GPA).
must_not: Stopping at the first step; no deadline. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

**Office of the Provost**
Under some limited circumstances, a student may appeal a grade. Circumstances for which students may appeal gradesGrade appeals will be considered only if a student can provide documentation supporting their case. Circumstances that might justify a grade appeal include (but are not limited to): computational error; factual information not in evidence at the time the grade was posted (for example, an assignment that the student can document was submitted but was not graded by the course instructor and therefore not factored into the final grade); or an alleged violation of College Policy. Appeals that will not be considered include, but are not limited to, those based on a student’s perceived need for a higher grade (for instance, in order to raise their GPA or to enable the course to transfer to another institution) and those based on grades that were penalized (for example, a sanction of a 0 on an assignment or an F in the course) because the student was found responsible for violating the Academic Integrity Policy. [2]
If circumstances such as those described above can be documented, the student may appeal a grade by taking the following steps: No later than twenty calendar days after the posting of grades, a student must bring their appeal to the attention of the course instructor in writing by email or certified letter. Supporting documentation must be provided. Both parties should make good faith efforts to share viewpoints and mediate differences of opinion. Students and instructors have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination of grade. If it is mutually agreed that a grade adjustment is warranted, the course instructor forwards an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request, including explanatory reasons and all supporting documentation, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course. Upon the Dean’s approval, the Instructor Grade Adjustment Request is forwarded to the Registrar. If a student and the course instructor cannot reach an agreement and a student wishes to further pursue a grade appeal, the student must present a written appeal (by email or certified letter), including pertinent course materials or course work, to the Dean of the academic unit which sponsored the course in question within twenty calendar days of the final determination conference between the student and the course instructor. The Dean will confer with the student and the course instructor, jointly or independently as they see fit, review pertinent documents and course materials, and confer with other faculty or administrative staff members as appropriate. If the Dean determines that a grade change is warranted, the Dean will forward an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request with explanatory reasons to the Registrar and advise the course instructor and student in writing. If the Dean determines that a grade change is not warranted, the course instructor and student will be so informed in writing by email. [3]

**Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [21]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [22]

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what gpa do you need to graduate cum laude
good_reply: Cum laude 3.500-3.699, magna cum laude 3.700-3.849, summa cum laude 3.850-4.000; the GPA is not rounded.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Cum laude requires a cumulative GPA of 3.500 – 3.699. The Office of the Provost awards Latin Honors to undergraduate students based on cumulative GPA at Ramapo College; the GPA is not rounded. [1]

The Registrar awards Latin Honors automatically to graduates: 3.500 – 3.699 for Cum Laude, 3.700 – 3.849 for Magna Cum Laude, and 3.850 – 4.000 for Summa Cum Laude. [9]

The Registrar awards Latin Honors automatically to undergraduate graduates based on cumulative GPA, including “R” grade credits: 3.500 – 3.699 cum laude, 3.700 – 3.849 magna cum laude, and 3.850 – 4.000 summa cum laude. Undergraduate Seniors with questions regarding Honors Program should consult the Honors Program Director at (201) 684-7110. [10]

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [15]

question: if i drop a class and go part time will i lose my financial aid
good_reply: Aid is adjusted below full time (12 credits): federal aid needs at least 6 credits; going from 12 to 6 reduces a Pell Grant but federal loans can be kept; state aid may be canceled; Ramapo grants and scholarships (merit scholarships need 12 credits) may be reduced or taken away. Talk to Financial Aid before dropping.
must_not: Leading with "I can't see your records" instead of the rules (a short note at the end is fine). Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Financial Aid:
- If you drop below full-time status, your financial aid will be adjusted. [1]
- Federal aid requires you to be enrolled in 6 credits in a semester. [1]
- If you go from full time status 12 credits to part time status 6 credits your federal pell will be reduced but you can keep your federal loans. [1]
- If you have state aid that is subject to being canceled and institutional grants and scholarships could also be reduced or taken away. [1]
- Federal aid should not be affected if a student is still enrolled for 6 or more credits. [2]
- NJ State aid (ie TAG, EOF, etc) requires that students be enrolled full time at the time the aid is fully disbursed to your account. [2]
- If you drop below full-time status which is less than 12 credits your Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be taken away or reduced for the semester. [3]
- Please contact the Office of Financial Aid to discuss your situation before making a change that drops you below full-time status for the semester. [3]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [12]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: im graduating in january, when is my graduation application due
good_reply: Nov 6, 2026 for the January 2027 conferral, still ahead on the day asked. The application goes through the Registrar.
must_not: A wrong date; calling the deadline passed.

body.answer:
November 6. Registrar: Graduation applications and all paperwork are due to the Graduation Office as follows: January graduation—November 6; June graduation—April 1st; August graduation—May 31st [1]. Fall: application available June 1 to November 6; deadline November 6; official conferral of degrees January 22, 2027; diploma mailed Mid-March; commencement ceremony date To Be Announced. Spring: application available October 15 to April 1; deadline April 1; official conferral of degrees June 17, 2027; diploma mailed Late July; commencement ceremony date To Be Announced. Summer: application available March 1 to May 31*; deadline May 31*; official conferral of degrees August 21, 2026; diploma mailed Late September; commencement ceremony date To Be Announced. *Graduation Applications received after April 1 will not be listed in the Commencement Program [3].

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i have a medical condition, how can i request a housing accommodation
good_reply: Step 1: register with OSS (Application for Affiliation plus documentation from a licensed provider). Step 2: the Housing Accommodation Student Request Form and Provider Documentation Form. Step 3: meet Residence Life's deadlines. A committee (OSS, Residence Life, Health, Counseling) decides within 21 business days of complete documentation. OSS: 201-684-7514, oss@ramapo.edu, C-205.
must_not: Leaving out a step. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
You can ask for support with that.

1. **Housing & Residence Life:** Any resident requesting specific housing accommodations due to a medically related condition must register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS). [1]
2. Submit housing accommodation requests no later than published deadlines. [1]
3. **Office of Specialized Services:** Students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with OSS. See “How To Request OSS Services” ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/)) for more information. Students must initiate contact with OSS to receive services or arrange accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [4]
4. Submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist to establish eligibility and determine appropriate accommodations and/or adjustments. [4]
5. Students requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms. They only need to complete a request for disability support form. [4]
6. Expect a decision within twenty one (21) business days of OSS receiving all requested documentation. [5] If the information is insufficient for OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee to determine whether an accommodation is necessary, OSS will inform the individual in writing that more information is needed and may request to speak directly with the professional supplying it. [5]
7. For a comprehensive description, refer to the Office of Specializes Services (OSS) Housing Accommodation Request Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf)). [6]
8. To assist a student with specific housing needs, the student must affiliate with OSS by providing documentation verifying the presence of a disability and need for the requested accommodation. [7] OSS staff and, in most cases, the Housing Accommodation Request Committee review the request. [7] Time is needed to complete this process. [7]

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [13]
- **Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/apply/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/frequently-asked-questions/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

citations.title: #1 - Register with the Office of Specialized Services

pageFacts.question: How can I request a housing accommodation for a medical condition?

facts.says: Any resident, who is requesting specific housing accommodations, due to a medically related condition, will need to register with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Please submit requests for housing accommodations no later than published deadlines.
All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with the Office of Specialized Services (OSS).
Check out our webpage “How To Request OSS Services” (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/how-to-request-oss-services/) for more information.
Students must initiate contact with OSS in order to receive services or to arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments.

Comprehensive documentation of a disability from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist must be submitted in order to establish eligibility and to determine which accommodations and/or adjustments are appropriate for each student.

Note: Students requesting only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor do not need to complete the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms, as below.
Students only need to complete a request for disability support form.
Students can expect a decision about their request within twenty one (21) business days of OSS receiving all requested documentation.

If the information provided does not contain sufficient information for OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee to determine whether an accommodation is necessary, OSS will inform the individual in writing that more information is needed and may request to speak directly with the professional supplying that information.

For a comprehensive description on how to request a housing accommodation please refer to the Office of Specializes Services (OSS) Housing Accommodation Request Policy (https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/wp-content/uploads/sites/137/2024/03/1-Housing-Accommodation-Request-Policy-updated-3-7-24.pdf).

A: In order to assist a student who has specific housing needs, the student must affiliate with OSS by providing documentation verifying the presence of a disability and the need for the requested accommodation.
The request is then reviewed by the OSS staff and in most cases the Housing Accommodation Request Committee.
Time is needed for this process to be completed.

question: can i have an emotional support animal in my dorm, and how does approval work
good_reply: Call OSS at 201-684-7514 and meet with the OSS Director; documentation from a health care or mental health professional is needed; the animal may come only after OSS approval (Residence Life pets rule); it may be limited to defined areas, generally not academic or recreational buildings.
must_not: Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Office of Specialized Services: It depends. Please call our office at 201-684-7514 to discuss your interest in having an Emotional Support Animal on campus. [1] Interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director to discuss further. [1] Please refer to the Emotional Support Animal Policy ([https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/)) for more information. [1] A student with a disability must register with OSS, provide disability documentation demonstrating the benefits provided by the emotional support animal, and be granted an accommodation permitting the animal on campus. [2] Use may be limited to defined areas of campus and generally will not be permitted in academic or recreational facilities. [2] The College is committed to accommodate students and others with disabilities that require service or support animals. [3] Animals are only allowed on campus when providing service or support to a College member or campus guest as a reasonable disability accommodation. [3] This policy applies to individuals with disabilities accompanied by a service animal or requiring a support animal on campus. [3] OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a requested accommodation if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented. [4] OSS together with the Housing Accommodation Request Committee shall determine if the requested accommodation is reasonable. [4] An accommodation may be deemed unreasonable if: 1) the student’s documented condition does not rise to the level of a disability; 2) documentation does not provide adequate evidence to support the request; 3) imposes an undue financial and or administrative burden on the college; 4) fundamentally alters college housing policy; 5) poses a direct threat to the health and safety of others or would cause substantial property damage to the property of others, including college property. [4] For an emotional support animal request, if applicable, the College may also inquire as to the animal’s age, size/breed to determine whether the accommodation is reasonable. [4] All students requesting a housing accommodation based on a disability must first register for affiliation with OSS. [5] Students must initiate contact with OSS to receive services or arrange appropriate accommodations and/or academic adjustments. [5]

**Office of Specialized Services**: Phone: (201) 684-7514. Email: oss@ramapo.edu. Location: C-Wing, Room 205. [16]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-accessibility-and-services-information/service-support-animal-policy/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/housing-accommodations/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: i got a parking ticket. how do i pay or appeal it and how long do i have
good_reply: Appeal online within 20 days of the citation (appeal form; reviewed by the Parking Appeals Board). A citation not paid or appealed within 20 days gets a $5 late fee (another $5 after 28 days), and the right to appeal is lost after 20 days. Payment as the page says.
must_not: Leaving out the 20-day limit. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
Public Safety: You have twenty (20) days from the citation’s issuance to appeal. [1]

1. Appeal online through the form: [https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3](https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3). [1] If you miss the twenty (20)-day deadline, you forfeit the right to appeal. [2] Appeals will not be considered for ignorance of the regulation; stated inability to find a legal parking space; operation of the vehicle by another person; stated failure of parking enforcement staff to ticket previously for similar offenses; inability to pay the fine; disagreement with Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations; or citations issued by the Mahwah Police Department. Identify the specific ground(s) for your appeal and briefly describe your justification. [2] Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee. [3] The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days. [3] A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days. [3]

2. Pay online at [https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx). Enter Citation # and Fine Amount, search for the citation, select your citation, and follow the field required. [4] Select Payment Method. Once processed your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid. [4]

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [13]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/vehicle-citation-information/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

pageFacts.question: How do I pay or appeal a parking ticket, and how long do I have?

facts.says: How to Appeal Your Parking Citation Click Here to Go to the Appeal Portal (https://cm.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=3) Appeals are input online via the form An online appeal by the owner/driver must be made within twenty (20) days of the issuance of a citation.
Failure to file the appeal within twenty (20) days constitutes forfeiture of the right to appeal.

Appeals will not be considered for: Ignorance of the regulation Stated inability to find a legal parking space Operation of the vehicle by another person Stated failure of parking enforcement staff to ticket previously for similar offenses Inability to pay the fine Disagreement with Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations Citations issued by the Mahwah Police Department Appellants must identify upon which specific ground(s) they are appealing and briefly describe their justification.
IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS: Citations not paid or appealed within 20 days are subject to a $5 late fee.
The ability to appeal is forfeit if the appeal is not submitted within 20 days.
A second $5 late fee may be assessed after 28 days.

How to Pay for Your Parking Citation Online Click Here to Go to the Payment Portal (https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/OCP/Main.aspx) Citations are paid online using the portal Enter Citation # and Fine Amount Search for Citation Select your Citation and follow the field required.
Select Payment Method Once processed your citation will be emailed to you to say that it is paid

question: when does the shuttle go to the mahwah train station
good_reply: The shuttle's times to the Mahwah station for the day asked, from the shuttle schedule.
must_not: Times from another day or route. Invented people, numbers, rooms or dates.

body.answer:
The posted timetable has no stop called “Mahwah train station”. The stops it lists are Ramsey Rt 17 Train, Garden State Plaza, Interstate Plaza, Ramsey Square, Barnes & Noble/Fashion Center, City MD Ramsey. The next shuttles today (Wednesday, November 4):
- 4:45 PM (Mid-Day Weekday Express Train), calling at Ramsey Rt 17 Train, back on campus at 5:27 PM
- 5:30 PM (Mid-Day Weekday Express Train), calling at Ramsey Rt 17 Train
- 6:10 PM (Weekday Roadrunner Express), calling at Ramsey Rt 17 Train, Interstate Plaza, City MD Ramsey, Garden State Plaza, Barnes & Noble/Fashion Center, Ramsey Square, back on campus at 7:35 PM
- 8:20 PM (Weekday Roadrunner Express), calling at Ramsey Rt 17 Train, Interstate Plaza, Garden State Plaza, Barnes & Noble/Fashion Center, Ramsey Square, back on campus at 9:35 PM
- 9:40 PM (Weekday Roadrunner Express), calling at Ramsey Rt 17 Train, Interstate Plaza, Garden State Plaza, back on campus at 10:45 PM

Every trip leaves from Ramapo College (Bradley Center).

question: how do i pay my student account bill online
good_reply: Log in to RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service), open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite and Make Payment; pay by electronic check (checking/savings) or credit/debit card via PayPath. Bills are eBills only; a monthly payment plan exists. Student Accounts: studentaccts@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7495.
must_not: Anything about the Accounting program.

body.answer:
Student Accounts:
1. Run an On-Demand Statement to view current, real-time account activity and balances. View the eBill statement to designate third parties (i.e. parents) as Authorized Users who can view the bill and make payments. It is the only place to make an online credit/debit card or ACH payment, enroll in a monthly payment plan, and access previous bills. [1]
2. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then Make Payment. Select the term and click Continue. Select Credit Card via PayPath and click Select; verify or modify the amount and click Continue to PayPath. Read the non-refundable service fee disclaimer, then click Continue. [6]
3. Review the payment amount and click Continue. Enter Credit/Debit Card Billing Information and click Continue. The data entered, including the PayPath service fee, will be displayed. [6]
4. The credit/debit card service fee is 3.0%, with a minimum fee of $3.00. [6]
5. Review entries; use Change Information if needed, Cancel if you do not want the transaction processed, or Submit to pay. Submission accepts the non-refundable service fee. Print the Payment Confirmation Page. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [6]
6. These payments can ONLY be made ON-LINE. [7]
7. Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then Make Payment. Select the term and click Continue. Select Electronic Check (checking/savings), then Select. Choose Checking or Savings, enter bank account information, and click Continue. To save the payment method, select the save option before continuing. Review the agreement and click I Agree. Review entries; use Change these values if needed, Cancel if you do not want the transaction processed, or Submit to pay. Print the Payment Confirmation Page. The College reserves the right to change costs, dates and procedures at its discretion. [8]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [13]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/methods/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
